camps.description: New metal horse-barn with 12' x 12' box stalls, outside runs, auto-waterers, outdoor arena and round pen. Lots of room for trailer parking and 3 electric pedestals for LQ trailers so you can stay with your horses. Bagged shavings are available. Reservations are appreciated but not required. Owner lives on site and we're open 24/7, so please call ahead if possible. Full services are available in Wellington. Location notes: Easy access off I-25. From north-bound I-25 --get off at Exit 278 (Wellington Exit) and take the northbound frontage road 2 miles. Turn right at the 3rd driveway from the stop sign, marked with a large white bucking horse sign. From South-bound I-25 --take Exit 281 (Owl Canyon exit), cross over the Interstate to take the NE Frontage road south approximately 1 1/2 miles. Our driveway is on the (left) east side and is about 1/8 mile long up to the cattleguard and barn-yard. We are convenient to "The Ranch" (Larimer Co Fair Grounds), CSU Veterinary Clinic, Greeley, Denver, & Cheyenne Rodeos. Please have Health Certificates and Coggins papers to satisify Colorado Regulations.

camps.name: Ivy Creek Campground
camps.description: This facility has 4 developed sites each with a picnic table and fireplace ring. It underwent a major remodel in 2010. There is a vault type toilet designed for the handicapped, but it is not wheelchair accessible. Sites 1 and 2 would accommodate small trailers or tents. There is a foot bridge that goes across Ivy Creek from a small parking lot to the developed camp units 3 & 4, which are suited only for small tent camping. Parking space tight but is ample. No firewood, drinking water or refuse receptacles are provided. This campground is considered to be remote and is normally not heavily used, yet it is very attractive with the free flowing creek, and open grassland nearby. This area looks very different now due to the removal of dead and dying trees, a result of the spruce beetle. The road into the campground is too narrow and rough for large trailers and RV’s. The campground is really more suitable for tents and popup camping trailers, as there are no long developed spurs or pull-throughs. Scroll Down to Information Center to see the individual campsite descriptions. This is also the site of the Ivy Creek Trailhead and Bulletin Board. All Parking for the trailhead users is outside the fenced in campground where there is a hitching rail and room for horse trailers. Ivy Creek Trail #805 goes into the Wilderness and provides the quickest route to Goose Lake. This is a trail open to foot and horse travel only. Here you will find district maps, Weminuche Wilderness maps and information and trail registration forms. 14 DAY CAMPING LIMIT. No Potable Water Single Site - $10/night Day use - $10 (picnicking) Fee envelopes and collection box located near the entrance.

camps.name: J Bar Equestrian, Brett Jordan
camps.description: We have a large 80' x 120' vinyl fenced paddocks with loafing sheds for overnight or weekly boarding. Large 150' x 200' arena available for riding. 10 acres pasture for turnout can be arranged as well. Dry RV camping available. Location notes: 1 mile west of Poncha Springs, CO on Hwy 50.

camps.name: Jacks Gulch Campground
camps.location: Arapaho & Roosevelt National Forests Pawnee NG
camps.description: *Heavily damaged by the Cameron Peak Fire. Remains closed in 2024 while engineering planning for reconstruction occurs. Jacks Gulch Campground is located adjacent to the Pingree Park Road (CR63E) and the Old Flowers Road. It is situated in a ponderosa pine forest setting with scattered clones of aspen. It is also an area that has abundant wild flowers at certain times of the camping season. The Columbine Loop has 27 sites with electrical hookups. This loop also provides access to 10 walk-in tent sites. The Yarrow Loop has 28 sites without electricity. A unique feature of this campground is an equestrian camp which has 5 sites, each with four horse stalls and room to accommodate a horse trailer. Each site contains a tent pad, fire grate and picnic table. Some sites within this campground have a bear locker. There is a hiking trail that circumnavigates the campground. A portion of this trail serves as a self-guided nature hike and offers a stunning view of the Mummy Range. Popular activities in this area include hiking, stream fishing, mountain biking, scenic driving and some four-wheel driving. View a campground map. View Columbine Loop map. A single site may hold up to eight people. Tents must fit on the pads provided. RVs, trailers or other vehicles must fit on the parking spur because driving or parking off road is not permitted. The parking length ranges from 30 to 80 feet. Check our campground table for fee informaton. (A $5 electric fee is included in price. The electric fee is not included in any discounts.) Interagency Senior, Interagency Access, Golden Age and Golden Access passes provide cardholders half price for basic campground fees. See Jacks Gulch Equestrian for other fees. Fees are discounted 25% when water is off.

camps.name: Jacks Gulch Equestrian
camps.location: Arapaho & Roosevelt National Forests Pawnee NG
camps.description: *Campground was heavily damaged during the Cameron Peak Fire. Remains closed in 2024 while engineering planning for reconstruction occurs. Jacks Gulch Equestrian Campground is part of Jacks Gulch Recreation area which has RV, tent and group campsites. A nature trail circles the entire area. The campground is situated in a ponderosa pine forest setting with scattered clones of aspen. There are five sites, each with four horse stalls and room to accommodate a horse trailer. Two of the sites are reservable. Each site contains a tent pad, fire grate and picnic table. Popular riding and hiking trails are easily accessed from this campground. Five horse camping sites are available in one loop -- small corrals provided. Please note: Only noxious weed-free hay is allowed on public lands in Colorado. A list of weed-free hay suppliers is available from the Colorado Department of Agriculture. Dispersed camping with horses is also an option. Check detailed fee information on www.recreation.gov or see general fees on our campground table. Fees are discounted 25% when water is off. Interagency Senior, Interagency Access, Golden Age and Golden Access passes provide cardholders half price for basic campground fees.

camps.name: Jim Olterman - Lone Cone SWA Horse Camp
camps.description: Colorado Parks and Wildlife identifies Jim Olterman/Lone Cone State Wildlife Area as a camping property. The official state recreation lands guide lists access by foot or horseback and facilities consisting of two horse corrals and campsites. Camping is restricted to licensed hunters during specified hunting seasons and adjacent days.

camps.name: Koda Ranch, Taryn White
camps.description: We are a family owned and operated Boarding, Horse hotel and petting zoo. 24/7 staff on sight. Our over night stays offer: $50. clean stall, shavings included with fresh water, fed by our hay and cleaned by our staff. $30. Clean stall, owner provided shavings and feed, cleaned by our staff, $20. Stripped stall, owner provided shavings and feed, owner cleans stall before leaving. Station to clean out trailer. $10 dry camp stay. We have water access hookup, and a trailer dump station. Lounge that offers a refrigerator with cold water, freezer if needed for cooler items, fresh coffee, kitchen, TV, and tables. Restroom access (no portable toilet). Location notes: 5 minutes off the Watkins I-70 exit

camps.name: Kruger Equestrian Campground
camps.description: Private camp. Details may change; please confirm horse access, availability, amenities, fees, and rules before travel.

camps.name: Lower Hermosa Campground
camps.description: The Lower Hermosa Campground has 19 sites. Although horses are not allowed in the campground, the adjacent Lower Hermosa Creek Trailhead has an area with a horse corral for overnight horse camping, as well as hitching posts. The parking lot is large enough for vehicles and horse trailers. Services include vault toliet, trash pickup, campfire grates, and picnic tables. Bear-safe food storage is recommended. Please note, there is no water available at this campground. • Quiet time is typically between 10pm - 6am. Please be a good neighbor and limit use of generators to no more than one hour at a time. • Dogs must be leashed or otherwise physically restrained. Do not leave pets unattended. • Check-out time: 12:00 pm; Check-in time: 2:00 pm - if the site is empty, campers may come in anytime. • Standard single site occupancy is 8, but a single family with > 8 members is acceptable. • Equipment with wheels (RVs, campers, cars) must fit in the parking spur. There is not any overflow parking available. • Max RV size = 30 ft $20

camps.name: Luders Creek Campground
camps.description: The campground has 5 sites, 3 are pull through. There are 3 corrals for horses and other stock. This is a good area for big game hunting season. Mountain biking & 4WD driving on area roads. The most common trees are Engelmann Spruce and quaking Aspen. The road leading to the campground is itself of historical significance. It was one of the famous toll roads leading west from Saguache built by Otto Mears in 1876. Attractions include big game hunting, other dirt roads and the Cochetopa Pass on the Continental Divide. Continental Divide Trail is found 1 mile west. Horse camping is allowed. Fires in designated fire rings only. Single site - $10/night. Day use - $10/day (picnicking). Fee envelopes and a collection box are provided near the entrance.

camps.name: M Lazy C Ranch
camps.description: Started as a homestead back in 1906, M Lazy Ranch is now a thriving guest ranch and cowboy playground. M Lazy C Ranch is the ideal location for a family trip, time with friends, romantic horse rides and more. Our original turn of the century Cabins dating back to that time period, have been lovingly restored. Not your typical dude ranch. We are flexible and offer a multitude of options to choose from. We also offer RV sites, Equestrian RV Sites, an Arena, Cabins, Weddings, Hunting, Events, and more! Surrounded by 350,000 acres of Pike National Forest on three sides provides our guests with unlimited riding potential and amazing views. Bring your horses or join one of our wranglers on a ride on our property for a perfect relaxing gateway the whole family can enjoy. Sit on the porch of your very own piece of heaven, relax, put your feet up, and stay awhile.

camps.name: MINGUS RANCH
camps.phone: FOR RESERVATIONS, CALL (877) 444-6777, FOR OTHER INFORMATION CALL (719) 489-3370 OR (719) 269-8500.
camps.description: Overview Mingus Ranch is a cabin where guests can step back in time and feel like they're staying on an early 20th century homestead. The cabin was built in 1908 and was operated by the same family for six decades before it became a Forest Service property. In collaboration with the Frontier Pathways Scenic and Historic Byway and the Colorado State Historical Society, the cabin and neighboring barn have been renovated to match their original appearance and filled with period-specific furniture and antiques. Electricity is provided and a horse corral is onsite. Recreation Hiking, mountain biking, horse riding, off-road vehicle riding, hunting and wildlife viewing are all enjoyable activities here. An extensive network of hiking trails and roads for biking are nearby. Facilities The modest two-story ranch building is an example of a typical high country ranch. The cabin sleeps six and conveniences include electric heat, an electric stove and minimal electric lighting. A vault toilet, picnic table and campfire ring are located outside, as well as a horse corral. Furnishings consist of one bunk bed, two single beds, a queen sized bed, a kitchen sink not equipped with running water, table and chairs and some cooking pots and utensils. No drinking water is available so it's important to bring plenty. Other items to bring include bedding, food, garbage bags, dish soap, sunscreen and other basic camping gear. There are minimal lights at the facility, so visitors please bring additional light sources. The outhouse is several hundred feet from the cabin. Please leave the cabin as clean as you have enjoyed for the next visitor. Natural Features The cabin is perched in a sprawling meadow at an elevation of 9,400 feet near the base of Round Top Mountain in the heart of the Wet Mountains. Surrounding the meadow are spruce and other mixed conifers. The scenic Greenhorn Mountain is due south. Nearby Attractions Westcliffe, a mountain town is 26 miles northwest of the cabin. The tow

camps.name: Mancos, Colorado, Hobo's Hideout Bed, Breakfast and Barn
camps.description: Large apartment with two queen beds, kitchen, satellite TV, private bath and covered patios. Freshly cooked breakfast included. LQ trailer parking with facilities to trailer. Four show barn stalls, shavings and hay provided, turn out, and small arena. Location notes: Seven miles north of Mancos, Colorado off Highway 184, on secluded 44 acres. Thousands of nearby acres of BLM and US Forest Service to ride.

camps.name: Marvine Campground
camps.description: This popular campground is located 36 miles east of Meeker, CO along Marvine Creek. It offers access to a number of trails and lakes within Flat Tops Wilderness and is a good base for hiking, fishing horseback riding and hunting. Marvine Trail #1823 and East Marvine Trail #1822 both begin near the campground. Marvine Campground has six horse campsites. The corrals for public use are at the horse camp sites in the campground; please note that the corrals at the Marvine Trailhead are for outfitter and guide use only. Additional facilities at the campground include tables, fire grates, vault toilets and hand pump drinking water. Livestock may be watered at the stream, about 200 yards from the campground. View Dates and Fees Only certified weed-free forage and bedding is allowed in the campground. The East Marvine and Marvine Trails lead into the Flat Tops Wilderness, where regulations apply

camps.name: Mimosa Ridge, LLC
camps.description: Private farm in Parker, CO (near Denver) available for overnight stays/short term boarding. 4 stall barn with runs, paddock turn out and arena available. Small rigs preferred. Hotels/restaurants within 2 miles or trailer camping allowed. Please call or email for more information. Location notes: Southeast of Demver.

camps.name: Mondorosa Bed & Barn
camps.location: 1250 Achy Back Lane, Canon City, CO 81212
camps.description: Four stalls, two cross-fenced pastures, three iron pipe runs, 420 acres of fenced in free range grazing pastures, 60 ft round pen. Well water, hay available for purchase. 3 bedroom, 2.5 bathroom ranch home available for short term rental through VRBO & AirBNB. 4,000 acres of trail riding available. No electrical hookups for RV, but well water is available to replenish holding tanks. Location notes: Mondorosa Ranch is an off-grid, working ranch located in Fremont County, 26 miles north of Canon City at 8,500 ft. elevation.

camps.name: Mueller State Park Equestrian Campsites
camps.description: Campsites 133 and 134 are equestrian sites. Equestrian campsite reservations must be made by phone at 1-800-244-5613. Equestrian Campsite Fee: $36 plus $10 per animal, per night, per site (two horses per site maximum)

camps.name: Outlaw Trails Ranch, John Hoyt
camps.description: We have a 15-horse barn with in and out stalls, or three large paddocks with cover for overnight camping. Horse overnight:$25/horse/night. Overnight camping: $25/night (dry camping), $30/night with utilities. Both choices include shower and outdoor kitchen use. Plenty of room for trailers with electric and water hookups. Bunkhouse use: $75/night. Trail access on property, large covered and open riding arenas, Derby field with jumps. Hay available for purchase. Dogs allowed on leash. Location notes: From Hwy 491 west on County Rd G. Located 4 miles from Cortez. Close to Mesa Verde and Four Corners.

camps.name: PALISADES HORSE CAMP
camps.description: Overview Palisades Horse Camp is located 30 miles north of Pagosa Springs, high in the San Juan National Forest. This beautiful area has excellent horseback riding and hiking trails and an abundance of wildlife. Recreation Hiking and horseback riding trails are the main attraction at Palisades. The Williams Creek Trail leads directly from the campground into the Weminuche Wilderness, crossing the Continental Divide. Facilities This equestrian campground offers single- and double-family campsites to campers with horses. Corrals with feeding bins are provided. The corrals are divided into two sections with room for two to three horses on each side, depending on horse temperaments. Hitching racks are set up throughout the campground and a water tank is on-site. Vault toilets and drinking water are provided. A campground host is on-site, and is very knowledgeable about the area. Natural Features The campground is nestled in a stand of pine, spruce and fir trees, and sits at an elevation of 8,300 feet. The area provides panoramic views of the surrounding meadows and mountains. Williams Creek flows nearby. The surrounding forest provides a prime wildlife habitat. Bears, deer, elk and moose frequent the area. Contact Info For facility specific information, please call (661) 702-1420. Charges & Cancellations Cancellations Individual Campsites: Cancellations up to 2 days before a reservation start date incur a $10.00 cancellation fee. A visitor who cancels a reservation the day before or on the day of arrival will pay a $10.00 service fee AND forfeit the first night's use fee including tax and applicable add-on for a campsite. Cancellations for a one-night reservation will forfeit the entire amount paid and will not be subject to an additional service fee. No-Shows A no-show visitor is one who does not arrive at a campground and does not cancel the reservation by check-out time on the day after the scheduled arrival date. Staff will hold a campsite until check-out time on th

camps.name: PURGATOIRE CAMPGROUND
camps.phone: FOR RESERVATIONS CALL (877) 444-6777, FOR OTHER NON REAL TIME INFORMATION CALL THE SAN CARLOS RANGER DISTRICT AT (719) 269-8500.
camps.description: Overview Purgatoire Campground is nestled near the headwaters of the Purgatoire River in the beautiful Culebra Range of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. The primitive campground is laid out on two loops. One is a large grassy meadow with sites that accommodate equestrian campers and one that is wooded with aspen and spruce. Constructed by the Youth Conservation Corp in 1976, Purgatoire was originally named Potato Patch Campground. The river provides nice fishing and a trailhead attracts hikers and horseback riders. Recreation The North Fork Trail # 1309 is located on the north end of the campground and offers non-motorized access to hikers, cyclists, and horseback riders. The 5-mile trail delights with mountain vistas and shade from forested terrain. The river, which is creek-sized at these upper reaches, provides opportunities for anglers to cast for trout. Facilities Campsites come with campfire rings, picnic tables and vault toilets. Equestrian sites can fit large horse trailers. Drinking water is from a hand pump and parking aprons are grass and gravel. Trash service is provided. Natural Features The campground is in an aspen and conifer forest near the North Fork River at an elevation of 9,800 feet. The river, also known as the Purgatoire River, flows 196 miles to the confluence of the Arkansas River. Pike-San Isabel National Forest includes over a million acres of wilderness and over half of Colorado's mountain peaks that reach above 14,000 feet. Contact Info For facility specific information, please call (719) 489-2034. Nearby Attractions The nearby towns of Stonewall and Cuchara offer shopping and restaurants. Charges & Cancellations Cancellations Individual Campsites: Cancellations up to 2 days before a reservation start date incur a $10.00 cancellation fee. A visitor who cancels a reservation the day before or on the day of arrival will pay a $10.00 service fee AND forfeit the first night's use fee including tax and applicable add-on for a campsite. Cancell

camps.name: Parker, Colorado, Sunset Pines
camps.description: 2 stalls. Rubber matting through barn and in stalls. Round pen. Pasture. Trailer space. Beautiful, private, cozy, quiet and safe location. Location notes: 12 miles east of Parker (12 minutes).

camps.name: Picket Wire Corrals Interpretive Site
camps.description: This popular meeting spot, about 33 miles south of La Junta, offers wildlife interpretation and corrals for public equestrian use.

camps.name: Pine River Campground
camps.description: Pine River Campground is located four miles beyond Middle Mountain Campground, at the end of Forest Rd. 602. The campground is adjacent to the trailhead for the Pine River Trail #523 This area is often used as a temporary base camp and parking area for hikers and backpackers. Campsites accommodate only tents or small RVs. All 6 campsites have views up the Pine River Valley. Private land adjoins the campground, with no public access to the river until three miles up the trail. There is no potable water. Although horses are not allowed in the primitive campground, the Pine River Trailhead has a parking area with a horse corral for overnight horse camping, as well as hitching posts and a turn-around parking area for trailers. • Quiet time is typically between 10pm - 6am. Please be a good neighbor and limit use of generators to no more than one hour at a time. • Dogs must be leashed or otherwise physically restrained. Do not leave pets unattended. • Check-out time: 12:00 pm; Check-in time: 2:00 pm - if the site is empty, campers may come in anytime. • Standard single site occupancy is 8, but a single family with > 8 members is acceptable. • Equipment with wheels (RVs, campers, cars) must fit in the parking spur. There is not any overflow parking available. • Max RV size = 16 ft $20

camps.name: Pueblo, Colorado, Greenhorn Horse Hotel
camps.description: We have 14 stalls that are 12' x 12'; most of them have runs attached. Two stud stalls. 4 pipe pens that are 12' x 42' and 8 pens that are 12' x 20'. There is a lighted 40 foot round pen and a 50' x100' lighted arena. There are 12-30 amp trailer hook ups and 2-50 amp hook ups. If you don't have living quarters there is a people motel just three miles from the barn. The large circle drive can accommodate any size rig from 4-18 wheels. We are open 24/7. Please call in advance if possible. Rates are $30.00 per horse. $30.00 for trailer hook up. Location notes: We are approximately 20 miles south of Pueblo on I-25. Exit #77 (Abbey Rd./Hatchet Ranch Rd.). We are on the west side of the Interstate. Entrance is on the sevice road. Look for sign.

camps.name: Raber Cow Camp Interpretive Hike
camps.location: Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Fore
camps.description: Raber Cow Camp is a loop trail with interpretive signs around an the old Historic cabins and corral. Most of the abandoned cow camps on the Grand Mesa were thought to be hazardous so the Forest Service tore them down. However, the Raber Cow Camp was spared and was actually renovated in 1993 as an example of what life here was like in the 1940’s and 1950’s, the heydays of cow camp life on Grand Mesa. Winifred Raber, who stayed at the cow camp every summer from the 1930s until 1966, has helped document the history of the camp. Some of her recollections and photographs are presented along a short interpretive trail that visitors can walk to learn about the cow camp’s history. The cabins were preserved in 1998 in partnership with the Colorado State Historic fund." More Information Map to Raber Cow Camp

camps.name: Ranch West, Savannah Whitford
camps.description: With your stay you would have the options for a paddock or a 10' x 10' stall with a private run that opens into a pasture with 2 other horses. $40/horse and hay is included. Barn is rustic and charming and about 20 minutes outside of the town of Steamboat Springs. An outdoor arena would be available for use and nearby trails are less than 5 miles away from the barn. Location notes: Southwest of Steamboat Springs.

camps.name: Ravens Roost Ranch, Gary Sibert
camps.description: 2023 new barn with (4) 12X12 matted box stalls with shavings connected to (4) 12X12 sheltered runs. One 4-acre paddock with 2 loafing sheds, large round pen and covered arena. Camera Security system in place and owners on premises. We have hay and water available, as well as 20, 30, 50 Amp hookup. Biosecurity: Current Coggins, and health certificate required. If possible, please use your own water and feed buckets. Owners' horses are housed in separate areas. Please keep dogs on a leash. Other amenities: Next door neighbor has an Airbnb: "Karen's Alpaca and Llama Ranch." Nearby Wellington has a motel, and full services. Close to CSU Vet Hospital, trail riding in Red Feathers lakes, and Cheyenne. Location notes: Easy access off I-25: exit Owl Canyon Rd (County Rd 70), 2 miles west to roundabout, then 5 miles north on NCR9. There is plenty of room to park and turn around for large rigs. Well lighted for evening arrivals. Please call for availability and pricing..

camps.name: Riding2horses Farm
camps.description: We've MOVED to a NEW Location. Same great service and improved facilities in Loveland, Colorado! We are just 15 minutes from The Ranch. 4 - 12' x 12' stalls with one bag of shavings included. Additional shavings at $10.00 per bag. Multiple turnout paddocks with loafing sheds - suitable for multiple horses with horse safe fencing. 2 arenas and roundpen. 30 amp RV hook up. Great big rig access. Location notes: Two miles west of I-25 and 15 minutes from The Ranch Event Center in Loveland.

camps.name: SEEDHOUSE GUARD STATION
camps.description: Overview Seedhouse Guard Station is located approximately 26 miles north of Steamboat Springs, Colorado. It was constructed in 1933 and offers a unique lodging opportunity for guests seeking recreation and relaxation in the Routt National Forest. This historic cabin is available for rent in the fall and winter. Guests can drive directly to the cabin when the roads are clear; however, winter access is only available by snowmobiling, cross-country skiing or snowshoeing over three miles from the end of the plowed road. The cabin offers some amenities, but guests need to pack in several of their own supplies. Recreation Trailheads leading to hiking and horseback riding trails are an easy drive from the guard station. The Continental Divide National Scenic Trail passes near the cabin through the Mt. Zirkel Wilderness. Anglers can fish for trout in the Elk River. In winter, the area is blanketed by snow for wintertime play. Snowmobiling, skiing and snowshoeing are popular activities. All motorized activity, including snowmobiling, is prohibited in wilderness areas. Facilities The historic guard station is furnished with two sets of bunkbeds with mattresses and can accommodate up to five guests (3 twin beds, 1 full bed). Other amenities include a propane range, refrigerator, lights, heater, table and chairs, cooking utensils and cookware. A campfire ring and a picnic table are located outside. An outhouse with vault toilet is nearby. Horses may be kept in the corral or in the pasture in the fall; however, fencing is not provided. Hay must be certified weed-free. Drinking water and electricity are not available. Guests must provide their own supply of water for cooking, cleaning and washing. In winter, there is a large pot provided for melting snow. Guests need to provide their own food, headlights or flashlights, sleeping bags, pillows, towels, dish soap, matches, first aid kit, toilet paper and garbage bags. All trash and food must be packed out, and guests are expected t

camps.name: Salt of the Earth Ranch, LLC, Chelsea Kiter
camps.description: We offer a 3 bed/3 bath one level home (Airbnb). Fully stocked kitchen, dining room, laundry appliances, woodstove, garage, and back patio overlooking the La Plata Mountains. Two paddocks available with LQ/RV hookups, water, shelter. Nightly layovers or short term boarding. 5th wheel rental next to paddocks available to rent. One queen, twin xl bunkbeds, one sofa pull out floor mattress. Small kitchen/dining/ shower-bath combo. Outdoor picnic area, fire pit, steps away from horse paddocks. I require a negative coggins test and health certificates. Equine Salt & Light wellness trailer on site: certified halotherapy, red light therapy, and photo-patch therapy. Location notes: Location: Minutes from 160 and 170. 30 minutes from downtown Durango. Mancos, Cortez, Pagosa Springs, New Mexico all within a short haul. San Juan National Forest and La Plata Canyon nearby. Private and quiet gaited ranch.

camps.name: Saul's Creek Stables
camps.description: Saul's Creek Stables is a full service operation to help you make the most of your time spent in Southwest Colorado. ​ We offer RV hook ups, horse facilites, and trails from our property on to National Forest.

camps.name: Soap Creek Campground - Gunnison RD
camps.location: Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Fore
camps.description: This campground provides access to the southern trails of the West Elk Wilderness. On site is Coal Mesa Trailhead, which is the portal for a network of trails including 451.2 (Coal Mesa), 451 and 452. Horse corrals and bins are located adjacent to the campground. 21 campsites. $18 per night per camping unit; $6 per day for day use/picnic use in a campsite; $10 per firewood bundle.

camps.name: Soap Creek Corral / Coal Mesa Horse Camp
camps.location: Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Fore
camps.description: Dispersed camping is available at the horse corrals located adjacent to the Soap Creek Campground. This campground provides access to the southern trails of the West Elk Wilderness. No fee

camps.name: South Fork Campgound
camps.location: Arapaho & Roosevelt National Forests Pawnee NG
camps.description: The South Fork Campground is a first-come, first-served campground located in the Williams Fork Valley. Facilities: There are 21 non-electric sites that will accommodate tents, trailers and RVs. Each site contains a tent pad, fire grate and picnic table. Additional facilities include restrooms, trash service and drinking water. The South Fork Campground is the only campground on the Sulphur Ranger District that is designated for horse camping. There is a small corral in the campground for one or two horses. No water troughs. Group campsite: South Fork Campground also has one non-electric group site that can hold up to 25 people. The group site may be reserved. Recreation: Popular activities include hiking and horseback riding on nearby trails and in the Byers Peak Wilderness area, where Wilderness regulations apply. View a COTREX map. View a campground map. • A single site may hold up to eight people. • Tents must fit on pads provided. RVs, trailers and other vehicles must fit on the parking spur. Driving or parking off road is not permitted. • Maximum Vehicle Length: 23' • Pets must be on a hand-held leash. Check the campground table for fee information.

camps.name: South Fork Group Site - Arapaho NF (CO)
camps.description: Overview South Fork Group Campground is located in north central Colorado in the Williams Fork Valley next to South Fork Creek. Many mountain streams and creeks nearby offer good fishing opportunities. South Fork is the only facility in the area designated for horse camping. Recreation The South Fork Trail begins at the campground and is one of the most popular trails in the valley. The 26-mile loop trail is open to hiking and horseback riding, and provides access to other trails in the area, including Ptarmigan Pass, Ute Peak and Jones Pass Trails. Mountain biking opportunities also exist in the valley. The Byers Peak Wilderness can be accessed nearby. Anglers enjoy trout fishing on the South Fork Creek and numerous additional streams and creeks in the surrounding area. Wildlife viewing opportunities abound. Facilities The campground offers one reservable, accessible group site that can accommodate up to 25 people. Individual sites are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Picnic tables, campfire rings and tents pads are provided, as are flush and pit toilets and drinking water. A small corral, for one or two horses, is located in the campground. Natural Features The campground is located in the Williams Fork Valley next to South Fork Creek at an elevation of 8,962 feet. A cool mountain climate with frequent afternoon thunderstorms should be expected. Due to the pine beetle infestation and hazardous tree removal, shade has been reduced throughout the campground. The Arapaho and Roosevelt National Forests and Pawnee National Grassland sit on the foothills and peaks of the Rocky Mountains in Colorado. The forests and grassland cover 1.5 million acres and extend north to the Wyoming border, south to Mount Evans and west across the Continental Divide. Charges & Cancellations Modifications for this campground must be made through Recreation.gov or by calling the call center at 1-877-444-6777 PRIOR to your reservation start date. Customers and contact center age

camps.name: State Forest State Park Bockman Campground Horse Camping
camps.description: Colorado Parks and Wildlife states that horse corrals are located at Bockman Campground in State Forest State Park, directly tying horse facilities to an overnight campground.

camps.name: State Line Stables
camps.description: We offer five 12' x 12' fully covered stalls with 13' x 50' paddocks off each run that are built with heavy duty pipe to ensure the safety of your horse while boarded with us. These stalls are matted and it's optional to purchase pine shavings. These stalls also have auto waterers as well! We also have five 8' x 12' semi-covered stalls with 12' x 40' paddocks. (These are not matted stalls) All stalls are lite with dusk to dawn lighting. There is an outdoor arena available for your use. We just ask that you supervise your horse(s) while they are out there and are not left unattended while in the arena (our arena is not currently fenced all the way around.) Dogs are allowed on the property as long as they are friendly and on a leash. The driveway on the property is a U shape, perfect to pull any size trailer/rig through. We have multiple full hook ups for trailers if you wish to stay in your trailer to be close to your horse. * trailer hookups are an additional fee * We live on premises and will greet you and your horses upon arrival. We will be available for any of your needs while you are with us. Our property also has camera coverage. We are open yearly 24/7 so please reach out for your boarding needs. We do require that you provide us with proof of negative Coggins test and health certificate for your horse(s) to be on the property. We offer nightly and monthly boarding. Please contact for pricing and availability. We offer multiple payment options to make it convenient for you while traveling. Location notes: Less then 2 miles off of I-70, just north of the the highway. We are located close to multiple fast food restaurants, a few sit down restaurants, Safeway, multiple hotels and multiple gas stations that will fit large rigs. Conveniently located near the I-70 exits and multiple smaller highways.

camps.name: Sunset Pines
camps.description: 2 stalls. Rubber matting through barn and in stalls. Round pen. Pasture. Trailer space. Beautiful, private, cozy, quiet and safe location. Location notes: 12 miles east of Parker (12 minutes).

camps.name: TNT Training and Arena, Mika Tozer
camps.description: 8 covered boarding stalls, Rv plug ins with water, Covered riding barn, Outdoor arena, with cattle and practices for extra cost, Calf roping lane, with cattle for extra cost. Training and sales offered as well. Location notes: TNT Training and Arena on Google maps.

camps.name: Tally Ho Horse Hotel, John & Nila Parrington
camps.description: Notice: We are closed to overnight guests from December through March. 3, 12' x 24' pens for $15.00/night, outdoors with no cover, with fresh water (heaters for winter). 2, 60' x 60' pens with shelter for $25.00/night. We usually can take 4 friendly horses in the bigger pens. Big rig accessible. Proof of negative Coggins test, current health certificate and brand inspection (for out of state travelers) required. Rooms for the traveler are $50.00 per night night. You can stay with us or not. We have electricity and water for campers. I'm not an official bed and breakfast but can rent rooms and offer our guests breakfast (and dinner, if you arrive around dinner time). Location notes: Easy access on and off I-70 at either Rifle Exit #87 (West Rifle Exit to avoid round-a-bouts with trailers) or Silt Exit #97. We are located on Antlers Lane (County Road 225) off U. S. Highways 6 & 24 just 3.5 miles from Silt or Rifle (just past mile marker #96 coming from Rifle). Call (try cell phone first) for reservations, rates, information and directions.

camps.name: Target Tree Campground
camps.description: Target Tree Campground, located between Durango and Mancos off Highway 160, has 28 sites on a south-facing hillside overlooking Thompson Park. There are 17 barrier-free sites. Many sites are shady, but can be hot on sunny days. Most large and pull-thru sites require mechanical leveling of RVs. Three campsites have corrals for overnight camping with horses. The campground's group campsite group site has been converted into individual sites and is no longer available as a group site. Services include potable water, trash pickup, composting vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire grates. There are no electrical hookups, dump station, firewood, or showers. • Quiet time is typically between 10pm - 6am. Please be a good neighbor and limit use of generators to no more than one hour at a time. • Dogs must be leashed or otherwise physically restrained. Do not leave pets unattended. • Check-out time: 12:00 pm; Check-in time: 2:00 pm - if the site is empty, campers may come in anytime. • Standard single site occupancy is 8, but a single family with > 8 members is acceptable. • Equipment with wheels (RVs, campers, cars) must fit in the parking spur. There is not any overflow parking available. • Max RV size = 45 ft Standard: $24

camps.name: Thirty Mile Campground
camps.description: Thirty Mile Campground is nestled on the banks of the Rio Grande, just a short mile from the Rio Grande Reservoir. The location is perfect for anyone who loves to spend time in the water, fishing, canoeing/kayaking and swimming. There is an Amphitheater where campfire programs are periodically presented during the summer and nature trails. There are two trailheads that take you into the Weminuche Wilderness. Climbing and backpacking/horse packing in the San Juan mountains. The campground is located in a wooded meadow situated between the Rio Grande and newly renamed Grizzly Creek with some sites overlooking the creek. All sites are nestled among mature spruce or Aspen trees. The campground is adjacent to the Weminuche Wilderness with two trailheads (newly renamed Grizzly Creek # 814 and Weminuche Pass # 818) that link to the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail and are accessed just below the Rio Grande Reservoir. This campground is very popular with both fishermen and hikers accessing a wilderness experience. Firewood is available for a fee. There is ample parking for fishermen and backpackers. No stock unloading or horse trailers are permitted, but 1/2 and 3/4 miles east, adjacent to Forest Road 250, pack stock can be unloaded and stock trailers can be parked near some public corrals. This is bear country; practice safe food storage techniques. Scroll down to Information Center to see individual campsite details. There is a 14-day stay limit. On Rio Grande Reservoir and Road Canyon Reservoirs, boats are allowed; no wakes, trolling motors OK. Primitive boat ramp Single site - $29 - $33/night. Double site - $58 - $62/night. Day use - $12/day (picnicking). Shoulder season - $10/night (Sometime after Labor Day weekend) Fee envelopes and a collection box are located near the entrance.

camps.name: Thor's Horse BnB and Icelandic Rescue
camps.description: Pasture, 60' roundpen (summers), or lot; grass hay and water provided. Trailer parking available. Health certificate(s) and negative Coggins test required. Location notes: Located 18.5 miles northwest of Steamboat Springs off hwy 129. There are 8.5 miles of gravel to travel. In the winter, a 4WD vehicle is recommended.

camps.name: Trappers Lake / Horse Thief Campground
camps.description: The Horse Thief Campground at Trappers Lake has 5 campsites. It is on the right side of the road as you travel south from the Trappers Lake Outlet area. It has corrals for livestock, and long spurs to accommodate large trailers. An RV dump station is available near the campground. Trappers Lake and area adjacent to the campground is within Flat Tops Wilderness, where regulations apply. View Dates and Fees • See: Blanco Ranger District and Flat Tops Wilderness Regulations • Only certified, weed-free hay is permitted in campgrounds. • No hay is allowed in Flat Tops Wilderness; please use certified weed free pellets or cubes. • Motorized boats and wheeled carts for boat transport are prohibited.

camps.name: Triangle T Arena LLC
camps.description: 12'x30' runs with shelter ($30) -12'x12' indoor stalls with run ($40) -Shared turn out pens (6 horses per) ($10/ horse) -Onsite Veterinarian -Programmable Hot walker -Indoor Arena -Outdoor Arena -30/50-amp RV Electric Hookups ($20) -Dry Camping ($10). We provide self and full care options for all of our amenities offered. Fully accessible for full tractor/ trailer set-ups, out of city limits, and a world of friendly faces. We have lots of room and a beautiful view to share. We would love to accommodate you and your 4-legged companions! Location notes: 2101 County Rd 245, New Castle, CO 81647

camps.name: Triple BBB Farm on 285
camps.description: 7 12' x 12' stalls, indoors ($25 per horse.). Ample pasture land or dry lots, as desired. 46' in diameter round pen. Circle drive can accommodate any size rig. Trailer hook-up available ($30/night) so you can stay with your horses.) or we have a one bedroom, fully equipped VRBO Cottage (kitchen, bathroom, living room) on site available for $110 per night. Sleeps 4 with one queen sized bed and 2 single beds in loft. Incredible views of Collegiate Peaks. Plenty of places to exercise or ride - the round pen, pastures, extensive circle drive, and long dirt/gravel road that leads to an archery range is also perfect for riding. Friendly dogs welcome. Owner lives on site, open 24/7, call ahead for accommodations. Health certificates and a negative Coggins for each horse must be provided to meet Colorado Regulations. Note:This is a non-smoking property. Can pay via Venmo, Paypal or cash. Location notes: Easy access east off Hwy. 285. Arriving from the north on 285 - watch for Chaffee County Landfill sign, go south 3/4 miles turn left off highway at 3 mailboxes. Arriving from the south on Hwy. 285 - look for the Heckla Junction turn, go beyond 1 mile north, turn right at three mailboxes. Look for sign with big arrows pointing into the ground, east side in a pasture, that's the farm.

camps.name: Turtle Creek Farm, LLC, Amy Tjardes
camps.description: We offer 6 oversized box stalls with large runs. They all have automatic waterers and rubber mats. One bag of shavings is provided per day of stay. We also have two 30 amp hook ups for those that want to stay with their horses. Our fees are: $40 per night per horse, $20 for LQ Trailer electrical hook up per night, trailer parking is free. Dogs are welcome if on a leash. We have dog runs with shelter too. We have boarded horses monthly for over 10 years and have decided to help those on the road with their horses instead. We have owned horses for nearly 50 years and still have some of ours on the place. Our Veterinarian has even referred people to us with lame horses due to the care we give. Location notes: We are east of I-25 off Highway 14. We are 3.5 - 8 miles from restaurants, hotels and gas stations. 11 miles from CSU Vet Hospital, 14 miles from The Ranch Facility in Loveland, 22 miles from Island Grove in Greeley, and 43 miles from Frontier Park in Cheyenne. Horsetooth Rock is 35 minutes, Lori State Park is 30 minutes, and Red Feather Lakes area is an hour away for Trail riding.

camps.name: Twin Rivers Cabins And RV Park
camps.description: Not a horse camp but will allow horses to stay in their pasture.

camps.name: Ute Lodge
camps.description: Guest Horse Corrals & Horseback Riding We offer corrals for your horses, hand-led pony rides for kids, or we work with Welder Ranch for trail rides and overnight trips.

camps.name: VALLECITO CAMPGROUND
camps.description: Overview Vallecito Campground is a very popular site and one of the largest within the San Juan National Forest. It sits on Vallecito Creek, adjacent to the Weminuche Wilderness. Visitors enjoy the area for its trail and fishing opportunities, which are part of a very scenic, natural setting. Recreation Vallecito Creek offers fishing for rainbow, cutthroat and brook trout. Anglers must use artificial flies and lures due to the creek's location within the wilderness area. The Vallecito Creek Trail begins at the campground entrance. This popular trail is open to hiking and horseback riding only and is a main access point to the Weminuche Wilderness. Parking is available at the trailhead. Hitching racks and a horse staging area with a loading ramp for livestock is on-site, but no overnight horse camping is allowed. Facilities The campground offers 80 single-family sites, a few of which have electric hookups. Sites are equipped with a picnic table and campfire ring. Vault toilets and drinking water are provided. Day-use picnic sites are located along the creek at the campground entrance and are available for a fee. Natural Features Vallecito, which is Spanish for "little valley," sits at an elevation of 8,000 feet, high in the beautiful San Juan Mountains. A forest of ponderosa pine, aspen and gambel oak trees covers the campground. Most sites are large and fairly level. Contact Info For facility specific information, please call (661) 702-1420. Nearby Attractions Vallecito Lake is located four miles from the campground and offers boating, water skiing, fishing and hiking opportunities, as well as beautiful scenery. Charges & Cancellations Cancellations Individual Campsites: Cancellations up to 2 days before a reservation start date incur a $10.00 cancellation fee. A visitor who cancels a reservation the day before or on the day of arrival will pay a $10.00 service fee AND forfeit the first night's use fee including tax and applicable add-on for a campsite. Cancellation

camps.name: Vega State Park Horse Camping
camps.description: Colorado Parks and Wildlife offers reservable horse corrals at Vega State Park for a per-horse nightly fee adjacent to Pioneer camping and cabins.

camps.name: WEST DOLORES CAMPGROUND
camps.description: Overview West Dolores Campground is located on the West Dolores Road (Forest Road 535), which branches north from Colorado Highway 145 about 20 miles northeast of Dolores. It is a great place to relax and enjoy the outdoors by hiking, biking and fishing. Recreation The West Dolores River offers fishing for brown, rainbow, cutthroat and brook trout. A day-use parking area is available on-site. Several parcels of private property are found along the river. Visitors are asked to stay on the trail and not trespass. Mountain biking is allowed on Forest Roads 532 and 535. Forest Service Trail 624 begins three miles south of the campground. Facilities West Dolores Campground, located approximately a mile north of Mavreeso Campground, has 18 campsites on 10 acres near the river. Most campsites are shady and level. There are 10 reservable campsites, 7 campsites with electrical hookups and several that are suitable for large RVs. A site near the restroom is designated for wheelchair access and has electricity. The campground also has 2 picnic areas. Natural Features The campground is situated on the banks of the West Dolores River, which has its headwaters in the nearby Lizard Head Wilderness. A shady forest of spruce, ponderosa pine and Douglas fir covers the campground. The campground is at an elevation of 7,800 feet. Contact Info For facility specific information, please call (661) 702-1420. Nearby Attractions Southwestern Colorado, part of the Four Corners region, contains more than 4,000 archaeological sites and 600 cliff dwellings. Mesa Verde National Park is an hour and a half south of the campground, close enough for a day trip. Other sites within the region include the Anasazi Heritage Center in Delores, Canyon of the Ancients and Hovenweep National Monument. Burro Bridge campground is loacated 19 miles north of the campground offering Horse camping and a trail from the campground into the Lizard Head Wilderness. Charges & Cancellations Cancellations Individual Camps

camps.name: WILLIAMS CREEK CAMPGROUND
camps.description: Overview This popular campground, 23 miles north of Pagosa Springs, Colorado, offers both shaded and sunny campsites with some located creek-side. Visitors enjoy the area for its fishing, all-terrain vehicle (ATV) riding, and scenic opportunities. Recreation The campground is one mile from Williams Reservoir, a popular fishing and kayaking spot. There are several ATV and hiking trails approximately one to five miles beyond the campground. Facilities The campground offers many single family sites, some with water and sewer hookups and many with views of the surrounding mountains. There are two double sites and one triple site, suitable for larger family gatherings. There are a few level pull-through and back-in sites appropriate for larger RVs. Vault toilets and drinking water are available. Firewood may be purchased from the camp host. Natural Features The campground is situated among cedar, aspen and ponderosa pines. Some sites are located on the banks of Williams Creek, which runs along the eastern edge of the campground; some have spectacular views of the surrounding mountains. Contact Info For facility specific information, please call (661) 702-1420. Nearby Attractions There are many fishing opportunities in the creek and in the nearby reservoir. A popular hike nearby is Piedra Falls, located a short distance from the campground. ATV enthusiasts enjoy Poison Park Road which is several miles from the campground, or traveling to East Fork Road to enjoy this four-wheel drive-only road to Silver Falls. Just a few miles north of Williams Creek Campground, is the Cimarrona Trail which begins across the road from its campground namesake. The Williams Creek Trail begins at the end of the Williams Creek Road, at the Palisades Horse Camp. Both run through the Weminuche Wilderness to connect with the Continental Divide Trail. In addition, the town of Pagosa Springs offers many festivals on the weekends and the hottest, deepest hot springs in the country. Charges & Cancell

camps.name: Weston, Colorado, Ironstar Outpost West
camps.description: Electric 40' x 40' corral. Lodging also available. Location notes: Close to San Isabel National Forest and approximately 40 miles away from Trinidad, Walsenburg, and La Veta.

camps.name: Winding River Resort
camps.description: Love to take your horse with you when you’re traveling? Winding River Resort is the perfect location for a horseback riding vacation. With your own horse, you have direct access to miles of designated trails in adjacent Rocky Mountain National Park or trailer your horses to more distant trail heads. You can even take a day trail ride through Rocky Mountain National Park over the Continental Divide to Estes Park, Colorado. At Winding River Resort, you can set up your own camp or stay in our lodge rooms and cabins. Horse runs are available on your campsite or at the barn. Covered barn runs are 16 X 24 and site runs are 16 x 32, large enough for two horses. Call us at 970-627-3215 for a reservation. Horse campsites are water & electric with pen, can hold up to 2 horses. Rates start at $105 per night, includes 2 adults and 2 horses/or mules. Sites 61, 63, 65, 67, 69, 71, 73, 75, 77, and 79 are the horse campsites with pen.

camps.name: Woods Lake Campground - Norwood RD
camps.location: Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Fore
camps.description: Woods Lake Campground is situated next to Woods Lake in a dense aspen forest. It has 3 loops with 41 campsites. The main loop has a group site, 4 double sites, and pull-through sites. The horse loop has 5 sites, 5 paddocks, 2 hay racks, watering troughs, pull-through sites and a large parking lot. This parking area is ideal for horse trailers and serves as a trailhead for the Woods Lake Trail. The campground is an excellent base camp for hikers and equestrians to access the Lizard Head Wilderness via the Lone Cone Trail or Woods Lake Trail. Mountain bikers and motorcyclists can access the Wilson Mesa Trail, only.5 miles from the campground. Fishing opportunities are within walking distance of the campground at nearby Woods Lake. The campground is surrounded by dramatic mountain views of the Lizard Head Wilderness. The "quaking" leaves and majestic fall colors from the aspen trees add to the campground's allure. Telluride, a full-service community, is located about 8 miles east on State Highway 145 from the Fall Creek Road intersection. $20 per night per camping unit; $22 per night for equestrian sites; $6 per day for day use/picnic in a campsite; $10 per firewood bundle.

camps.name: Candlelight Farms Inn and the Hangar at Candlelight Farms
camps.location: 214 Candlewood Mountain Road, New Milford , CT 06776
camps.description: Overnight accommodations for you and your horses...Stalls and/or grass turnout. We are dog friendly!!!! Room for the whole family! Breakfast before you roll out!!!! Pricing is $200.00 for one horse and one room in our Inn. $30.00 per additional horse for paddock, and $40 if in need of a stall. Hay and water will be there....Room for a large rig to turn around and easy in out. Easiest if arrival is during daylight if possible. Location notes: 214 Candlewwod Mountain Road, New Milford, CT 06776

camps.name: Natchaug State Forest - Silvermine Horse Camp
camps.description: Silvermine Horse Camp. Offers 15 wooded sites. Basic facilities only - campers are responsible for cleaning sites and carrying out all trash. No water available, campers must provide their own water. Pet permitted. The campground is located on State lands that are open to hunting No fee. Available on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations. 2026 season: Opens Friday, April 10 and closes Thanksgiving Day.

camps.name: Pachaug State Forest - Frog Hollow Horse Camp
camps.description: Frog Hollow Horse Camp. Offers 18 semi-wooded sites. Two composting toilets available. Sites are available on a first-come, first-served basis. Reservations are not available. Campsite fees paid on site. Pet permitted. The campground is located on State lands that are open to hunting $17/night/campsite for CT residents $27/night/campsite for non-CT residents 2026 season: Opens Friday, April 10 and closes Monday, October 12.

camps.name: S & A Farm, LLC, Sandy Turmel
camps.description: Box stalls, limited paddocks, round pen. We have direct access to trails, including Larkin Trail. We are a quiet, drama free facility. We have ample parking and easy access for any size truck & trailer. We are within minutes of hotels, restaurants, and fuel stations. Several Equine Veterinarians are within a short distance, should they be needed. Location notes: We are conveniently located 1.5 miles from Interstate 84. If you have a larger rig, Bristol Town Road is not recommended. Continue to Route 67 & Hawley Road, then continue with GPS.

camps.name: Silver Bear Farm, Joan Adams
camps.description: Large run-in shed with paddock, tack room, hay room, lower barn with stall and small paddock, round pen and small ring, pasture also available. All fencing is board or fence panels. Electric and water in barns. Plenty of parking for trailer and turn around. Quiet area in the country. Location notes: East of Hartford and north of New London.

camps.name: Boone's Farm, Eve Boone
camps.description: 2 barn stalls 12' x 12' and 10' x 12', one pasture that does have my 5 horses over the fence. Run in. Hose and extension cord is all I can offer live in trailers besides parking. Hay for sale. Round pen. I have a little 4 acre farmette that I keep my 3 horses and 2 minis on. All horses are friendly, vaccinated and don't leave home. They would be able to mingle over the fence line but if stalled, they'd never interact. I can also rent humans my house, 2 bedroom, 2 baths available, but I would be by at 7am and 5pm to feed only. Thanks for looking! Location notes: About 40 minutes away from the Atlantic Ocean where you could ride your horses on the beach in the off season. Plenty of local trails to haul to. 1.5 hours to Fair Hill. 10 minutes to Harrington race track.

camps.name: Iona Stables and Inn, Linda Muncy
camps.description: We offer a full-service bed and breakfast. We also offer nightly rental for horses with serval options. 1) Pasture and run 2) pasture only, and 3) stalls at the barn with riding rink. The riding rink is outside. There is parking for horse trailers. Location notes: Southeast of Milford and convenient to Route 1, Slaughter Beach, and the Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge.

camps.name: Lums Pond State Park Equestrian Camping Area
camps.description: Conservative Delaware State Parks first pass. Official Lums Pond State Park information surfaces both equestrian trails and camping at the park, so it is included as a likely horse-friendly overnight option to verify before arrival.

camps.name: Trap Pond State Park Equestrian Camping Area
camps.description: Conservative Delaware State Parks first pass. Official Trap Pond State Park information surfaces equestrian use and family camping at the park, so it is included as a likely horse-friendly overnight option to verify before arrival.

camps.name: Alafia River State Park
camps.description: Florida DEP currently lists this park as offering equestrian camping. Park status: Open. Other camping status: Open.

camps.name: Anthony, Florida, Dusty Rose Farm
camps.description: 42 13' x 13' - 14' x 17' matted stalls with automatic waterers. Brand new 4 board fencing for turnout. Climate controlled tack, feed, and bathroom. H/C wash rack. Full RV hookups. 80ft and 60ft roundpen, 200' x 170' fibre arena, grass dressage court, grass jump field, 1/2mile sand track. Accessible to any size rig/semi. Location notes: 20 minutes from downtown Ocala, 15 minutes from Highway 75.

camps.name: Bear Head Hammock Horse Camping
camps.description: Florida Forest Service identifies primitive campsites with horse stalls at Bear Head Hammock in Withlacoochee State Forest, adjacent to the 8.4-mile equestrian trail.

camps.name: Black Horse Resort Ranch
camps.description: Private camp. Details may change; please confirm horse access, availability, amenities, fees, and rules before travel.

camps.name: Brooksville, Florida, Spotted Dance Ranch
camps.description: Cottage that can sleep up to four, trailer hookups (30-amp electric and water), covered stalls (10' x 10', 10' x 20', 12' x 14'), paddocks, stall/paddock combinations, water, wash racks. Location notes: Just west of I-75 at Exit 301. After getting off at Exit 301, take Highway 50/Cortez Blvd. west for 2 miles to High Corner Road, turn right onto High Corner Road and head north, after about a mile, curve to the right onto paved Wildlife Lane, after about a mile, turn right onto private Fannin Hill Road, our driveway is the first one on the right. Do NOT use GPS to get to our ranch; it will take you down small dirt roads not suitable for horse trailers!

camps.name: Buckman Lock - St. Johns Loop South Equestrian Camp
camps.description: Florida State Parks documents 12 primitive equestrian campsites at St. Johns Loop South beside Buckman Lock, with high tie posts at each site and access to multi-use trails.

camps.name: Coastal Haven Stables, Caren Martino
camps.description: We have walk-out stalls for guest boarders, $25/night. 50 foot diameter round pen. 150' x 450' outdoor arena with jumps and obstacles such as a tire mountain, a noodle "wall", a seesaw, bridges, a fabric "wall", horizontal noodles, vertical noodles to name a few. Access directly from rear of property to Eglin Reservation which offers hundreds of square miles of trail rides (some rules apply, contact us for further details, annual recreation permit is $20). Tacking stations with washing capability. Public restroom (no shower). Trailer parking available, but no camping hookups. Two Airbnb cabins to rent: 1 bedroom, 1 bath, sleeps 4. See listings on Airbnb for availability and prices: Lake Cabin and Stable Cabin. We are only 20 to 30 minutes from the best beaches in Florida! Trail ride one day then the next day have a fun day in the sun and sand on the Destin and South Walton Beaches and leave your horse(s) in our walk-out stalls. Location notes: On State Highway 20 midway between Niceville, FL (south on State Hwy 285 or State Hwy 85 from I-10, Crestview) and Freeport, FL (south on State Hwy 331, from I-10, DeFuniak Springs).

camps.name: Colt Creek State Park
camps.description: Florida DEP currently lists this park as offering equestrian camping. Park status: Open. Other camping status: Open.

camps.name: Cozy Cabin
camps.description: Cypress 600 ft. Cowboy Cabin - completely private on 5 acres. Totally furnished with: Tempur-pedic queen bed. Cute kitchen, New 8' x 10' bathroom with circular shower and Kohler sink and toilet. 1/8th acre paddock looking out on multi-acre tree farm. Down our street is a 28,000 acre forest with horse trails, hiking trails, bicycle trails AND, the Withalacoochee River nearby. 5 rivers within 30 minutes of the cabin. Safe, quiet and secure. Required rental: one month or more, 2 horses, 2 persons. $2,200 per month, $300 damage deposit. Includes electric, water, laundry service, internet. Guest must supply all hay and feed. Location notes: In Hernando County, FL - Brooksville, Fl. 4 miles to 7-11 and the historic town of Brooksville. 8 miles to a Walmart and fast food alley and other services.

camps.name: DOE LAKE GROUP SITE
camps.description: Overview Doe Lake is a group campsite with a variety of activities. Centered around a historic lodge with a large group kitchen, it's an ideal place for major outdoor gatherings of up to 250 people. The site is a favorite among equestrian groups, but can also accommodate weddings and other social events. Please read before making reservations Doe Lake Rules and Regulations Agreement For reservations or refund request please call (877) 444-6777 Recreation Equestrian camping, canoeing, boating and fishing are some of the popular activities around Doe Lake, and can be enjoyed exclusively by visitors with a group reservation. Campers can launch a canoe or low-powered boat and drop a line in the middle of Doe Lake for an afternoon of fishing. Facilities This site is centered around a classic 1930s Civilian Conservation Corps dining hall that has been historically restored. Tent camping is most common at this facility. RVs and horse trailers are allowed, but limited to specific areas that do not offer hookups. Restrooms with flush toilets and showers are provided, as are hitching posts for horses. Natural Features Located in north central Florida, the Ocala National Forest spans four counties and 383,000 acres. It is the southernmost and oldest national forest east of the Mississippi River and protects the world's largest contiguous sand pine scrub forest. The camping area sits beneath a shady grove of oaks and pines overlooking Doe Lake, and the dining hall sits atop a grassy hill with a view of the water. Nearby Attractions The Ocala National Forest is notable for its extensive off-road trail system catering to both ATV enthusiasts and Jeeps, as well as being a traditional destination for deer hunters. These opportunities are available in designated areas throughout the forest.

camps.name: Durham Farms, Lynda Matthews
camps.description: Electric (30 amp and 50 amp service) available. Water hook up available for horse trailers with living quarters or RVs. 3 stall barn or 5 acres pasture available. If needed, hay is available. Pets are okay and there is a fenced in run area for them. We require a valid coggins certificate. $40.00 for trailer/RV hookup and $25 per horse a night. We have an outside fire pit where you can watch beautiful sunsets and relax. Sorry, no stallions accepted. Location notes: approximately 10 miles south of Live Oak, FL. camps.name: Lake Delancy West OHV Campground
camps.description: Lake Delancy West is an OHV recreation area along Lake Delancy that houses OHV corrals, access to numerous marked OHV trails along the Ocala North OHV Trail System and camping along the lake. The recreation area also serves as a trailhead and designated campground along the hiking-only Florida Trail. Camping • Tent and small trailer camping is available at 30 sites within the pine forest along the western shore of Lake Delancy. All sites are within close proximity to the OHV corral, the Ocala North OHV Trail System and the Florida Trail. Heads up: Bears do frequent this area. You are required to store your food in a bear-proof container or in your vehicle. Fishing • We provide access to the lakeshore marshes for fishing. Perfect for tossing one on the fire for dinner while camping. Hiking • Backpackers use the Lake Delancy West Recreation Area as a designated campground along the Florida Trail. The campground is 0.3 mile from the main trail. Segments of the Florida Trail run north and south of this point: North heads from Lake Delancy to Rodman Reservoir and south runs to Salt Springs. OHV Riding • OHV riders are welcome to camp at Lake Delancy, the major entrance point for the Ocala North OHV Trail System. A large OHV corral outside of the campground area gives you a place to park your ATV at night. Picnicking • Day users can enjoy a picnic with a view of Lake Delancy while sitting under the shade of the longleaf pines. • OHV riders must remain on trails marked for their use. • All Ocala National Forest campgrounds allow pets, but they must be kept on a leash no longer than six feet and are not permitted in designated swimming and picnicking areas. • There is a maximum stay limit of 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.

camps.name: WILLIS KNOB HORSE CAMP
camps.description: Overview Located in the northern Georgia mountains, far from civilization, Willis Knob Horse Campground is one of the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forests most beloved horse-lover hideaways. The campground features equestrian camping, riding and hiking trails and fishing in the nearby Chattooga River. Recreation The 15-mile Willis Knob Trail in Georgia and 12.5 mile Rocky Gap Trail in South Carolina provide some of the most scenic horseback riding and hiking in the southern Blue Ridge Mountains. Winding across deeply dissected ridges, the trails descend into the vast Chattooga River. The 10.7-mile Chattooga River Trail and the 37-mile Bartram Trail are also accessible nearby and are for hiking only. Fishing is available in the Chattooga River. Facilities The campground provides single, double and group campsites for tent and RV camping. There are water and electric hookups at each of the horse campsites, along with tables, lantern posts and campfire rings with grills. Accessible vault toilets and drinking water are also provided. Sorry there is no dump station. The closest one is at Black Rock State Park in Mountain City, GA. Hitching highlines and a horse watering station are available. Campers are required to clean up after their horses using trailers provided on-site for manure only. Natural Features The horse camp is located in a heavily wooded area of the forest, amid deep canyons and near to the Georgia-South Carolina border. Nearby Attractions Chattooga River Wild and Scenic area is nearby Contact Info For facility specific information, please call (706) 754-6221.
