camps.name: Jerome, Idaho, Sugar Loaf Arena
camps.description: 10 12' x 40' covered paddocks, 12 box stalls, 12' x 12', 12' x 16', 16' x 16', 68' x 150' indoor arena, outdoor arenas. bathroom. We have an RV electric hook up and can easily accommodates large rigs.

camps.name: Jumbo Camp Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Recreation Region: Highway 14 Corridor Jumbo Camp Campground This high-elevation campground is situated in lodgepole pine near a flat, open area in an historic gold mining area. It is often used by horse enthusiasts and hunters and has a pit toilet.

camps.name: Kennally Creek Campground
camps.description: Kennally Creek Campground is situated in a serene setting among mature forest along the banks of Kennally Creek. Each of 11 sites include a fire ring and picnic table. A stock loading ramp and hitching rails are available at the site. Potable water is typically available June - September. All sites are available on a first-come, first-serve basis and camping is limited to an 14 day stay. The Interagency Pass and Golden Age Passport are accepted at this site. There are no hookups or trash receptacles. Please pack out your trash. The North Fork Kennally Creek Trail #102, East Fork Kennally Creek Trail #099, and the Needles Summit Trail #101 depart immediately from the campground with additional trail access just a few miles down the road. Kennally Creek Campground Recreation Opportunity Guide PDF $10/night

camps.name: LAKE CLEVELAND - EAST SIDE
camps.description: Overview Lake Cleveland Campground is a very popular summer recreational facility. Located next to its namesake, the campground is divided into the East Side and West Side loops. Very popular with residents of local communities, the campground is often full every weekend from early July to Labor Day. Recreation Fishing, kayaking, hiking and swimming are all popular activities within the Lake Cleveland area during the summer months. Non-motorized boating and floating is allowed on Lake Cleveland. Motorized recreation is limited to system roads and trails; no cross-country motorized travel is allowed. Facilities Seventeen camping sites are located in the East campground loop, seven of which are reservable, the remaining ten are first-come, first-served. The East side of the lake is best suited for large RVs and trailers. Nine campsites are available on the West side of the lake on a first-come, first-served basis. Trailers are not advised on the West side of the lake because the turn-around is very tight (limited space due to steep terrain). Natural Features At an elevation of 8,300 feet, the campground facility is located in an alpine lake basin below Mt. Harrison which has an elevation of 9,240 feet. Late season snowdrifts on the county road and in the campground often block access until early to mid-July. The campground is near the timberline and alpine wildflower meadows. Expansive views north across the Snake River Plain and south into Utah and Nevada can be found near the campground. Nearby Attractions Two miles from Lake Cleveland, Mt. Harrison has a fully functional fire lookout tower. Nearby Pomerelle ski area offers lift-served access to mountain bike and hiking trails. Two miles away, Twin Lakes Campground offers equestrian facilities and access to the Skyline Trail which is open for hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking and dirt bikes.

camps.name: Lake Cleveland Campground - West Side
camps.description: Lake Cleveland Campground is a very popular summer recreational facility. Located next to its namesake, the campground is divided into the East Side and West Side loops. Very popular with residents of local communities, the campground is often full every weekend from early July to Labor Day. Natural Features: At an elevation of 8,300 feet, the campground facility is located in an alpine lake basin below Mt. Harrison which has an elevation of 9,240 feet. Late season snowdrifts often block access to the campground until early to mid-July. The campground is near the timberline and alpine wildflower meadows. Expansive views north across the Snake River Plain and south into Utah and Nevada can be found near the campground. Recreation: Fishing, hiking and swimming are all popular activities within the Lake Cleveland area during the summer months. Non-motorized boating and floating is allowed on Lake Cleveland. Motorized recreation is limited to system roads and trails; no cross-country motorized travel is allowed. Facilities: Seventeen camping sites are located in the East campground loop, seven of which are reservable, the remaining ten are first-come, first-served. The East side of the lake is best suited for large RVs and trailers. Nine campsites are available on the West side of the lake on a first-come, first-served basis. Trailers are not advised on the West side of the lake because the turn-around is very tight (limited space due to steep terrain). Nearby Attractions: Two miles from Lake Cleveland, Mt. Harrison has a fully functional fire lookout tower which is open to visitors on most weekends. Nearby Pomerelle ski area offers lift-served access to mountain bike and hiking trails. Two miles away, Twin Lakes Campground offers equestrian facilities and access to the Skyline Trail which is open for hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking and motorcycle riding.

camps.name: Laughing Horse Ranch, Risa Roe
camps.phone: 208-941-1367 (If no answer please text!) or alternate/emergency contact Jami at 208-870-2131
camps.description: Welcome to Laughing Horse - Horse Motel. Peaceful, clean, and convenient overnight accommodations for horses and humans alike. For Your Horse: * Spacious 12' x 24' clean covered pens with wood chip footing * Optional non covered 25' x 25' open pen * Double-gated secure enclosure for safety and peace of mind * Lighted posts for easy after-hours arrivals * Water buckets and feed bins provided upon request * No stall cleaning required by travelers - just settle in and rest easy. For You: * Dry Camping: $35/night * Camping with electricity: $40/night (water included; no sewer or grey water dump) * Cozy Lodging: $80/night in a clean trailer with: o Queen bed + pull-out couch (sleeps 4) o Microwave, toaster, coffee maker, plates & silverware o Heated & A/C for year-round comfort o Just 15 feet from a bathroom with running water (no shower) Rates: $25 per horse * $35 dry camping * $40 electric hookup * $80 trailer lodging per night * We take venmo, paypal or cash or check in the cashbox * Late arrivals and early departures are no problem! 24 hours self-service. Location notes: Directions: (best to put our farm name in your GPS) From 84, head south on Eagle Road. Cross Lake Hazel Road, We are on the right hand side. The Motel Stalls are located behind the Big Shop past the hay stack on your right with the Laughing Horse Sign! Homesite option: I will give those directions as needed!

camps.name: Line Creek Stock Camp
camps.description: Line Creek Stock Camp features 9 pull through units for stock trailers, feed bunks and hitchposts, trailhead parking, and vault toilets. There is no developed water. Attractions include fishing in wild trout waters, beginning of wild portion of St. Joe Wild and Scenic River, and St. Joe River Trailhead. $10/ night. $5 additional fee for third vehicle

camps.name: Lower Penstemon Campground
camps.description: Lower Penstemon Campground is located 27 miles south of Hansen, ID on Rock Creek Road/County Rd. G3. The campground is located next to the Fourth Fork of Rock Creek (the main fork). There are 7 single family/individual sites in the campground. Camping fees are $8.00 per night. Sites can be reserved through Recreation.gov. Individual sites reserved through Recreation.gov will be posted. Sites that are not reserved are available on a first-come first-serve basis. Be sure a site is not reserved before you occupy. First-come first-serve customers must pay within 1/2 hour of occupying the campsite. Some sites are ADA accessible. Lower Penstemon is generally open from late May through October. Picnic tables, fire-rings, and 2 double vault toilets are available. The campground is well suited for medium sized motor homes, trailers and tent camping. This area is popular in summer for trout fishing, hiking, and wildlife watching. OHV vehicles can be use to enter or exit the campground. Recreational riding within the campground is not permitted. Many miles of ATV/ORV trails can be accessed to the south. Consult the MVUM (Motor Vehicle Use Map) for roads and trails open to your type of ORV (ATV, Motorcycle, etc.) No water is available at this site. Occupancy: The following act is prohibited within the Minidoka Ranger District: Pursuant to 36 CFR 262.58 (a), camping in any area including a developed recreation site or an undeveloped/dispersed recreation site for more than 14 (fourteen) days in a 28 (twenty-eight) day period. A camper or a group of persons camping together must move off of National Forest lands within the Minidoka Ranger District for a minimum of 14 days after camping for 14 days. Campers who remain longer than 14 consecutive days and/or camp more than 14 days within a 28 day period may receive violation notices and fines under the authority described under Special Order Number: 0414-01-028. For more information contact the Minidoka Ranger District Office in Burley, ID—208-678-0430. No Horses are allowed in the campground. Horse camping is provided in Loop E of Porcupine Springs, approximately 5 miles south (up canyon) from Lower Penstemon. Limit 2 vehicles (autos) per site. Vehicles must be parked on gravel spurs provided. Do not park on the road; do not block traffic. This is a fee campground. Fee envelopes and a collection box are provided near the entrance.

camps.name: MEADOW CREEK CABIN
camps.description: Overview Meadow Creek Cabin was originally built in the early 1920s and used as a guard station, which consists of five buildings. The main cabin contains the office, a sleeping area and the kitchen. The bunkhouse contains a main room and loft. There is also a tack shed, woodshed and outhouse. Since 1932, Meadow Creek has served as a workstation, with field crews occasionally utilizing the bunkhouse. The cabin is nestled among the pines on a steep-sided canyon along Meadow Creek. Plan on a 15-mile hike or horseback ride to this remote backcountry cabin, which is typically available from May 1 to September 15. Recreation Several trails are available in the area to explore by foot or horseback, including the Meadow Creek National Recreation Trail and the Butte Creek Trail. Anglers can enjoy fly fishing for trout in Meadow Creek after July 1st each year. Facilities The rustic cabin has six beds with mattresses, a living room with wood heat, and kitchen facilities with a wood cook stove. A propane refrigerator, dishes, cookware, kitchen utensils, Coleman lantern (no fuel provided), mop, bucket, broom, fire extinguisher and lights are provided. Modern bathroom facilities and electricity are not available. An outhouse is located near the cabin. An indoor but untested water system is available; all water should be filtered or boiled for five minutes. The propane tank is located on the back porch. A corral is provided for stock use and any grazing should take place beyond the grassy area in front of the cabins. Visitors must being weed-free feed for their stock. Visitors should bring garbage bags for packing out trash. The cabin does not have matches, bedding, flashlights, first aid supplies or Coleman fuel. Click here for more information about this cabin. Natural Features Meadow Creek is a major tributary of the Selway River and is known for its clean, cold water and unspoiled beauty. Big game species found in the area include black bear, elk, moose, mule deer, whitetail

camps.name: MINK CREEK GROUP SITE CAMPGROUND
camps.description: Overview Mink Creek Group Site Campground is located just 12 miles south of Pocatello, Idaho, along the Bannock Highway. The Mink Creek area is a popular area for birding and wildlife viewing, with many miles of multi-use trails waiting to be explored. Recreation The West Fork Mink Creek Trail begins just outside the campground and is popular with hikers, mountain bikers and horseback riders. Additional trails including Corral Creek Trail and Valve House Trail are in the vicinity. Facilities The campground offers one large accessible group site that can accommodate up to 200 people. The site contains a 40x80-foot picnic pavilion with concrete base, large paved parking area, 12 large picnic tables, two serving tables and a large fire ring, two accessible vault toilets and four potable water hydrants. The pavilion has two electrical outlets and night lighting. The road to the campground is paved, allowing easy access for RVs and cars. Security is provided by a locked entrance gate, area campground hosts and periodic county sheriff patrols. Mink Creek Group Area is popular for outdoor weddings; if you plan to move any site furniture please call Pinnacle Parks LLC for approval at (208)757-3999. Remember that site check-in time is 2:00 pm on the day of your reservation and check-out time is noon of the following day. Firewood is not provided and is not available on site for gathering. Garbage service is not provided. Mink Creek Group Site is managed by Pinnacle Parks Llc under a special use permit with the Caribou-Targhee National Forest. For questions please contact 208-757-3999 between the hours of 8am and 9pm. Natural Features The campground is situated along Mink Creek in the scenic Bannock Mountain Range of southeastern Idaho. A grove of ponderosa pines borders one side of the site, offering partial shade. Aspens and pines dot the surrounding mountainsides. A wide variety of birds can be found in the area, including the Western Scrub-Jay, Juniper Titmouse, Bushtit,

camps.name: Magruder Crossing Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Events Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Recreation Region: West Fork Ranger District Magruder Crossing Campground Current Conditions Closed annually by snow. Magruder Crossing Campground features 4 campsites on the Selway River, and a vault toilet. Stock can be kept in this campground. This was the crossing on a route established for commerce between Lewiston and Virginia City, MT during the gold rush. To the north of the campground, an earlier route, Southern Nez Perce Trail, crosses the road. Magruder Crossing Campground Sites located at Magruder Crossing Campground

camps.name: Mammoth Springs Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Recreation Region: St. Joe River Region Mammoth Springs Campground Mammoth Springs Campground features 8 camp units and vault toilets. Please observe the Pack it In Pack it Out refuse policy. Attractions include Dismal Lake (1 mile, on private timber ground). This campground was recently improved through a grant through an Idaho Department of Parks and Recreation.

camps.name: Mill Creek Trailhead & Campground
camps.description: Mill Creek Campground and Trailhead consists six camp sites available in a wooded setting along scenic Mill Creek. There is one accessible vault toilet, hitching rail, and unloading ramp. No Water is available. Nearby areas of interest include Mill Creek Lake National Recreation Trail, Mill Creek Lake and Firebox Meadows. $5.00/Night for single unit

camps.name: Mini Acres Farm, Ron George
camps.description: Large private shaded RV parking area. Covered 12' x 12' stall with a 12' x 60' run. Grass hay fed twice a day. 75' x 160' sanded arena. Grazing pasture. A pleasant, quiet little farm with lots of trees and grassy par-like areas. Location notes: Located approximately 30 minutes northwest of Boise.

camps.name: Nampa, Idaho, Dunn Rite Ranch
camps.description: Covered 20' x 20' stalls (not enclosed), arena, round pen, and wash area. Hay is available if you need it. For people, we have 3 RV hookups for LQ horse trailers with 30 AMP hookups, or areas for dry camping. Please go to our website to request a reservation for horses and/or people. Location notes: We are within easy access to I-84, Garrity Exit. We're in a rural neighborhood, close to services and the Ford Idaho Horse Park.

camps.name: North Fork Campground - St Charles Canyon, ID
camps.description: North Fork Campground is located in scenic St. Charles Canyon in southern Idaho, near Bear Lake. Visitors enjoy hiking, biking, horseback riding and motorcycling on local trails, and fishing in St. Charles Creek. Natural Features: A dense, mixed growth conifer forest covers the campground. St. Charles Creek flows gently through the site. Recreation: North Fork Trail, which has a trailhead within the campground, is open to motorcycles, horses, hikers and mountain bikers and connects with the Highline Trail, a 55-mile path along the backbone of the surrounding Wasatch Mountains. The Idaho Department of Fish and Game manages the river fisheries, providing excellent fishing most of the year, including in St. Charles Creek. In-season big game hunting is also a popular activity. Facilities: The campground offers an accessible group site that can accommodate a maximum of 50 guests. The group site is made up of five smaller sites. Picnic tables and campfire rings are provided, as are vault toilets. Roads and parking spurs are gravel. Nearby Attractions: Minnetonka Cave is a short distance from the campground. Scenic Canyons offers guided, 90-minute tours through the nine-room cave with formations called the Bride and Groom, Three Sisters and Devil's Kingdom. The cave temperature is 40 degrees and the path through it includes 444 steps. Tickets must be purchased at the cave entrance. Bear Lake's North Beach is 12 miles from the campground, offering swimming and fishing opportunities on one of the Inter-mountain West's largest natural lakes. Bear Lake State Park Marina is 20 miles from the campground, with a seven-lane boat ramp, boat rentals, slips, a snack bar and general store. Open after season, First Come/First Served; No fee, No Toilets, No Water For current fees, please go to Recreation.gov Open after season, First Come/First Served; No fee, No Toilets, No Water

camps.name: PADDY FLAT GUARD STATION
camps.description: Overview The Paddy Flat Guard Station is located in the Payette National Forest of central Idaho. Guests enjoy the remote area for its hunting opportunities and abundance of hiking, biking, horseback riding and off-highway vehicle roads and trails. Abundant streams and numerous alpine lakes within travel distance offer fantastic fishing opportunities. Recreation The Paddy Flat Guard Station serves as an excellent jumping-off point for adventures via horseback, motorcycle, ATV or hiking. Numerous trailheads within a few miles allow access to alpine lakes for fishing, meadows for watching birds and wildlife, as well as peaks ranging as high as 8,681 foot elevation for excellent views of the South Fork of the Salmon River drainage. Facilities Two cabins are available for rental at this guard station. Please be respectful of visitors at the adjacent cabin. The cabins were fully renovated in 2024. • Limited kitchen utensils such as dished and silverware are provided, but please bring your own so you have what you need. • The Guard Station is a "Pack-It-In, Pack-It-Out" facility. All garbage/trash must leave with you. Please clean up after use. • Pets are allowed, however please be sure to clean up after and maintain control of your animal. • Administrative buildings on site are not available for use. • Firewood gathering is available in the forest areas surrounding the Paddy Flat Guard Station, although none is provided on site. Do not bring firewood that is not local to the area. Don't Move Firewood! Help prevent the spread of tree-killing pests in our National Forests by obtaining firewood in proximity to your destination and burning it on-site. For more information visit dontmovefirewood.org. • No camping at the guard station. If camping is desired, Kennally Creek Campground, and a number of dispersed campsites are nearby. Cabin East • The occupancy within the Cabin East is four people. The unit is fully accessible and includes an access ramp off the backdoor. The bat

camps.name: Paradise Campground
camps.description: Paradise Campground is located near the Paradise Boating Site which is one of the most popular launching sites on the Selway River. The campground consists of 11 sites complete with picnic tables, and fire rings. Other facilities include 3 vault toilets, hitching rails, and feed bunks. Campground can accommodate RV's or trailers to 25 feet.

camps.name: Paris Springs Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Discover History Explore the Forest! Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Closed Paris Springs Campground Paris Springs Campground is nestled along the banks of Paris Creek in Paris Canyon, about five miles west of Paris, Idaho. Tucked within the Caribou-Targhee National Forest near the Bear River Range, this campground sits at an elevation of 6,600 feet, accessible via County Roads 421 and 427 off U.S. Highway 89. Natural Features: The gentle Paris Creek meanders nearby, bordered by dense stands of pines and aspens that cast cool shade in summer and glow with color in fall. Wildflowers dot the landscape during warmer months, enhancing the area’s serene beauty. Numerous hiking, biking, and off-road vehicle trails crisscross the region, including access to the 55-mile Highline National Recreation Trail, offering ample chances to explore the rugged splendor of southeast Idaho’s high country. Facilities: The campground provides seven single-family sites and three group sites, each furnished with picnic tables and campfire rings. Vault toilets and drinking water are available. Roads and parking spurs are dirt or gravel. Season: Late May-Early September After Season: Open, first-come/first-served; no fee, no toilets, no water. Paris Springs Campgrounds

camps.name: Poet Creek Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Open Recreation Region: Magruder Road Corridor Poet Creek Campground Current Conditions Open year-round, but might not be accessible because of snow. Poet Creek Campground is situated in tall timber and has four camp pads, fire rings, and picnic tables. Four stock mangers are located south of the campground.

camps.name: Porcupine Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Discover History Explore the Forest! Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Closed Porcupine Campground Porcupine Campground is nestled along the banks of St. Charles Creek in St. Charles Canyon, about seven miles west of St. Charles, Idaho. Located within the Caribou-Targhee National Forest near Bear Lake, this campground sits at an elevation of 6,300 feet, accessible via Forest Road 412 off U.S. Highway 89. Natural Features: The gentle St. Charles Creek flows nearby, lined with pines and aspens that provide partial shade in summer and a splash of color in fall. Summer wildflowers brighten the forested canyon, creating a picturesque setting close to Bear Lake’s turquoise waters. Numerous hiking, biking, and off-road vehicle trails wind through the area, including access to the 55-mile Highline National Recreation Trail, offering endless opportunities to explore the stunning southeast Idaho landscape. Facilities: The campground provides six single-family sites and one group site for up to 20 people, each equipped with picnic tables and campfire rings. Vault toilets and drinking water are available, and roads within the campground are paved. A host may be present at a nearby campground. Season: Late May-Early September After Season: Open, first-come/first-served; no fee, no toilets, no water. Porcupine Campground

camps.name: Porcupine Springs Campground
camps.description: Porcupine Springs Campground is a developed campground composed of 12 individual units and 3 group units. One group area can accommodate up to 100 people and 1 group area can accommodate up to 50 people. This is a fee campground and reservations are required for group camping only. Fee envelopes and a collection box are provided near the campground entrance. This area is suitable for trailer and tent camping and it is accessible for a season that varies usually between June and September. Campground amenities include water faucets, toilets, and an accessible Stock Transfer Station. Little Fork Trailhead (#163) is located at the campground and is an easy multi-use trail that accesses an extensive trail system. There is an additional trailhead at the end of Forest Road 504. Loop A is composed of 4 single and 2 double sites and one 2 unit toilet. Loop B is composed of 3 single sites, 3 double sites, one 2 unit toilet, and a horseman area. Loop C is composed of 3 single and 3 double sites and one 2 unit toilet. Loop D is composed of 18 new family units with faucets, and two 2 unit accessible toilets. The parking lot can accommodate up to 8 RVs. Occupancy: The following act is prohibited within the Minidoka Ranger District: Pursuant to 36 CFR 262.58 (a), camping in any area including a developed recreation site or an undeveloped/dispersed recreation site for more than 14 (fourteen) days in a 28 (twenty-eight) day period. A camper or a group of persons camping together must move off of National Forest lands within the Minidoka Ranger District for a minimum of 14 days after camping for 14 days. Campers who remain longer than 14 consecutive days and/or camp more than 14 days within a 28 day period may receive violation notices and fines under the authority described under Special Order Number: 0414-01-028. For more information contact the Minidoka Ranger District Office in Burley, ID 208-678-0430. No Horses are allowed in the campground. Limit 2 vehicles (autos) per site. Vehicles must be parked on gravel spurs provided. Do not park on the road; do not block traffic. FEE AREA- Double Units $14.00/night Single Units $10.00/night Group Reservation Area $75.00/night Loops A, B, & C are reserved through www.recreation.gov as well as 4 single sites in Loop D

camps.name: Poverty Flat Campground
camps.description: Located along side the South Fork Salmon River, this paved campground offers 10 campsites, including 4 walk in tent sites. Hitching posts at each site. The campground serves as take-out for those floating the South Fork of the Salmon River from Goat Creek. Serves as the trailhead for an extensive trail system. Many loop hikes are possible from here, of varying lengths and difficulties, inlcuding Blackmare Creek Trail (#100) which start in the campground. Open to those on foot, horses, mountain bikes, and trail bikes. Fishing in the river. Fire rings, hitching rails, toilet, drinking water, pack in/pack out. Please pack out all your trash. No hook-ups. $10 single units

camps.name: Power Plant Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Partially Closed Recreation Region: Idaho City Ranger District Power Plant Campground Current Conditions Campground accessible until closed by snow, but no water or toilet cleaning service provided. The Power Plant Campground is near Atlanta, Idaho. A trailhead offers access to the Sawtooth Wilderness, heading northeast into a lake-filled basin. The historic mining town of Atlanta is just south of the campground. Good fishing in the river for rainbow trout and whitefish. For site specific questions, contact the Idaho City Ranger District.

camps.name: Race Creek Campground
camps.description: Three camp sites on the Upper Selway River. Boat put-in below Selway Falls. A trailhead at the campground goes east along the Selway River, providing access to the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness. Stock facilities are available for equestrians. The wild and scenic section of the Selway contains Class IV rapids and runs from Paradise Campground to Selway Falls. Very difficult for persons with disabilities to access. No Fee.

camps.name: Rafter H Arena & Horse Hotel
camps.location: 8221 S Ten Mile Road, Meridian , ID 83642
camps.description: We are a clean and safe, gated facility. Large, covered stalls or turn out pens with shelter, 30A/50A RV hookup, arena and round pen, big rig friendly. Location notes: Boise Idaho area. Easy access, 4 miles south of I-84 in Meridian, ID, close to the Idaho Center, shopping and restaurants.

camps.name: Rathdrum, Idaho, Silent Pines Ranch
camps.location: 20496 N Silent Pines Road, Rathdrum , ID 83858
camps.description: Peaceful horse accommodations located just minutes from Highway 41 in Rathdrum, Idaho. Silent Pines Ranch offers safe, spacious overnight and short-term boarding for traveling horses as well as longer-term arrangements when available. Amenities include: * Large pastures * Secure stalls with attached 50' x 140' runs * Round pen for exercise and turnoutm * Fresh water and quality hay available * Easy trailer access and parking * Quiet, family-owned horse property. We prioritize the health and safety of all horses on the property. Current Coggins and Health Certificate are required prior to arrival. Whether you're passing through North Idaho or looking for a comfortable place for your horse to stay, Silent Pines Ranch provides a clean, welcoming environment with experienced horse care. Location notes: North of Coeur d'Alene.

camps.name: Red Mailbox Campsite
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Open Recreation Region: Magruder Road Corridor Red Mailbox Campsite Heavily used by hunters, Red Mailbox Campsite provides camp pads, a corral and loading ramp. The site got its name from the historic, large red "mailbox" at the site which was used to deliver mail to outlying ranchers in years past.

camps.name: Redfish Corrals
camps.description: Guided horseback rides through the Sawtooth Wilderness.

camps.name: Riggins, Idaho, Davis home and land LLC, Nathaniel Davis
camps.description: 3 stalls, Rv 30 amp, Water, Arena. Location notes: 1 1/2 miles south on Hwy 95 south of Riggins.

camps.name: Rupert, Idaho, Broken H Ranch
camps.description: Overnight horse boarding. $15/night/horse. Seven 12' x 24' stalls with 12' x 12' covered/inside of barn. All stalls have feed and water buckets. Arena and wash rack are available. Hay and/or cubes are available on site for purchase. Power/water RV hookups for an additional $20/night. Or dry camp for free. Owners live on site, 24/7 access available Location notes: 7 miles north of I-84.

camps.name: SHORTY PEAK LOOKOUT
camps.description: Overview Shorty Peak Lookout, 45 miles northwest of Bonners Ferry, sits atop Shorty Peak with views of the Selkirk and Purcell mountain ranges of Northern Idaho, Montana, and British Columbia. The rustic dwelling was once used to patrol forest fires, and is now a unique way for overnight guests to escape the city and become enthralled with 360 degree views of area's magnificence. Access requires a moderate to steep 2.5 mile hike with a 1,300 foot elevation gain. The lookout was refurbished in 2005 and is in excellent condition. Recreation The 2.5 mile hike up to Shorty Peak is part of the fun of staying at the cabin. The trail is also open to horseback riding. While here, landscape photography and wildlife viewing are popular pastimes. Birding is particularly popular and guests may have the chance to look down on some birds of prey. Look for red-tailed hawks, golden eagles, and goshawks soaring over the valleys. Clear nights offer prime stargazing opportunities. Facilities The 15' X 15' cabin sits atop a 5 foot foundation and can accommodate two overnight guests. The look of the interior is modern with hardwood floors. Two twin beds with pads, two chairs, two tables, a historic fire finder, and a district map are included inside the cabin. A pit toilet is within 100 yards of the lookout. No drinking water or electricity is available. Guests are asked to bring plenty of water, food, bedding, a first aid kit and all other basic camp gear. Horses are allowed, but no corrals or hitching racks are available. Hobbles are recommended for horses. Natural Features Shorty Peak lookout is located in the Lower Kootenai River Area (Bonners Ferry District) of the Idaho Panhandle National Forest. The land is bordered by the Purcell and Cabinet Ranges and the Montana Line on the east, the rugged Selkirk Range on the west, and the Canadian border to the north. The 360-degree unobstructed vista from Shorty Peak Lookout is exceptional, with views of Kootenai Valley, U.S. and Canadian

camps.name: SNYDER GUARD STATION (ID)
camps.description: Overview Snyder Guard station, located on the banks of the scenic Moyie River, has been listed on the National Register for Historic places since 1982. The complex of seven buildings includes a residence, two log cabins, a cookhouse, warehouse, corrals, a machinery shed and a garage. The facility is spread across 10 lovely acres and is perfect for large groups of up to 70 people or small family getaways. The buildings on the property were constructed from 1906 to 1936, and most structures are available for rent. A group picnic and camping area provide additional campsites and amenities for six RVs, plenty of room for tent camping, pathways to the river, and more. Snyder was originally constructed as a remote work station for early Forest Service employees. As roads were constructed and transportation improved, the site no longer required live-in crews, so visitors can now use these buildings as recreation rentals. Recreation Outdoor recreational opportunities abound on the Moyie River and nearby lakes. Fishing, whitewater rafting, canoeing and kayaking are all popular pastimes. Over 70 miles of trails are open to hikers, mountain bikers, horseback riders, and motorcyclists. The Copper Falls viewpoint trail is just a few miles from the Snyder Guard Station on copper Falls Road #2517. Hunting, huckleberry picking, cross country skiing and snowmobiling are enjoyed in season. Facilities Historic Site buildings include the main ranger house, two small log cabins, a cookhouse, a horse pole barn, and several administrative buildings. Camping Loop buildings include a 50' x 30' covered picnic shelter, a camping loop with six sites with picnic tables and fire rings, a vault toilet, and additional parking for 10 vehicles. Additionally, two horse corrals, vault toilets, drinking water faucets, campfire rings, picnic tables, and a mowed grassy playing field are available for use. The ranger house has three bedrooms, a bathroom with a flush toilet and hot shower (low capacity, on

camps.name: SQUIRREL MEADOWS CABIN
camps.description: Overview Squirrel Meadows Cabin is located 24 miles east of Ashton, Idaho, just off the Ashton-Flagg Ranch Road. The current cabin was built in 1934, but the site has been used for administrative purposes since 1907. It's listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Only one other cabin in Wyoming was constructed with the same building plan. The 2-room cabin is made of lodgepole pine and features a wood shingled roof. Guests can drive to the cabin from mid-May through mid-November, although about 10 miles of the trip are on gravel roads. Snowmobiles and cross-country skis are required to access the cabin from approximately early December through mid-May. The trek from the nearest available parking at the snowmobile trailhead to the cabin is 10 miles. Recreation The cabin provides access to a variety of year-round recreational activities, including horseback riding, cross-country skiing and snowshoeing. Berry picking is available in late summer. Some of the other activities located within a few miles include off-road vehicle and motorcycle riding, snowmobiling, hiking and mountain biking. Game and game bird hunting is a popular pastime in season. Facilities This cabin sleeps six and provides bunkbeds, mattresses, a wood stove for cooking, table and chairs, and firewood. A hand pump, vault toilet, picnic table and horse corrals are located outside. Electricity is not provided. Guests may wish to bring battery or propane-powered lighting. Bedding, matches, and emergency items like a first aid kit are not provided. Trash bags are needed to pack out garbage. Natural Features Squirrel Meadows Cabin is situated at 6,500 feet on the Yellowstone Plateau of southwest Wyoming. The cabin sits in a meadow surrounded by pine trees. Guests can enjoy views of the distant mountains. Wildlife in the area includes black bear, wolf, elk, moose, mule deer, and grizzly bear. Nearby Attractions

camps.name: Secesh Campground
camps.description: Forested four-unit campground at 4,250' in a beautiful setting along the banks of the Secesh River. All five sites includes a picnic table and fire ring. Hitching rails are available for stock use. All sites are available on a first-come, first-serve basis. There are no hookups or trash receptacles. Please pack out your trash. Designated parking for the Secesh River Trail #080 is located along the access road to this campground. The trail departs from Lick Creek Road on the east side of the Secesh River. $10/night

camps.name: Slims Camp
camps.description: Slims Camp has picnic areas, toilet and three RV/Trailer pads. Access is very difficult for persons with disabilities. This site is off the main road, has fishing access and access to Meadow Creek National Recreation Trail. Stock facilities available for equestrians. No Fee.

camps.name: Snake River Arena, Ron Foster
camps.description: 22 indoor stalls. Shavings and cleaning are included with boarding. $30/night/horse. 2 50' x 60' outdoor pens available with automatic waterer. Patrons are welcome to use wash bays, restrooms, washer and dryer, indoor and outdoor arenas. 5 RV hookups available with water and electricity. 2.8 miles from I-15. There is a large parking lot for your rigs and easy to get to while traveling. 24 hour video surveillance on stalls. Centrally located to some of the prettiest country in the state. If you are looking for a place to rest your horses and keep them safe, look no further. The staff at Snake River Arena are experienced with horse care and boarding. Let us help with your traveling needs. Reservations can be made on our website. Location notes: Horse corrals, riding arena, full RV hook-ups. Beautiful Blackfoot, Idaho. 2.8 miles from Interstate 15. Centrally located to some of the prettiest country in the state.

camps.name: THOMPSON FLAT
camps.description: Overview Thompson Flat Campground is located high in the Albion Mountain Range of southern Idaho, near the towns of Declo and Albion. Visitors enjoy the area for its abundant trails, alpine lakes and scenic beauty. Recreation The Twin Lakes Campground area is located just outside the campground and across the road. It offers picnic areas, horse corrals and access to a variety of trails. Lake Cleveland is a two-mile drive from the campground, offering fishing, canoeing and trail opportunities. Several additional hiking, mountain biking, horse and off-road vehicle trails are on the mountain. Facilities The campground contains three group sites, which can accommodate from 40 to 64 people, respectively. All sites are equipped with large picnic tables and campfire rings with grills. There are four reservable single units and four double unit campsites as well as 17 additional single-family campsites that are available on a first-come, first-served basis, but the group sites must be reserved. Accessible vault toilets are provided. A campground host is located on-site. Roads and parking spurs within the campground are gravel. Natural Features The campground is situated in a beautiful wildflower-filled meadow lined with tall pine and fir trees, on the eastern slope of Mount Harrison. It sits at an elevation of 8,400 feet. Nearby Attractions A visit up the road to the Mount Harrison Lookout offers interesting area information and breathtaking panoramic views of the valleys below. Pomerelle Ski Area, just below Thompson Flat, offers lift-served hiking and mountain biking, scenic chairlift rides and a few dining options, generally on weekends.

camps.name: Table Meadows Campground
camps.description: Situated in a popular big game hunting area, Table Meadows Campground offers two toilets, two stock feeding bunks, a loading ramp, hitching rail and six camp pads. The West Fork of the American River flows through the campground.

camps.name: Table Meadows Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Open Recreation Region: Highway 14 Corridor Table Meadows Campground Current Conditions Open year-round, but might not be accessible because of snow. Situated in a popular big game hunting area, Table Meadows Campground offers 1 toilet and 1 fire ring. The West Fork of the American River flows through the campground.

camps.name: Ten Mile
camps.description: This campsite is the trailhead for Ten Mile Creek Trail #415 and sports a loading ramp, hitching rail, toilet and two camping pads. Ten Mile Creek flows through the campsite. Garbage services not available. Pack It In, Pack It Out. No Fee.

camps.name: Teton County Fairgrounds
camps.description: Private camp. Details may change; please confirm horse access, availability, amenities, fees, and rules before travel.

camps.name: Twin Lakes Campground (Albion Division)
camps.description: Please contact the Minidoka Ranger District for updated information at 208-678-0430. Twin Lakes Picnic and Campground is a fee, non-reservation campground that can accommodate 100 visitors. The area is suitable for tent camping. The area is accessible for a season that varies usually between July through October. Amenities include toilets, fire rings, and tables, and three horse corrals. Water is not available. The campground provides access to the Skyline (# 513). The Skyline Trail is 26.2 miles in length. The trail begins at the back of the campground and ends at the City of Rocks National Reserve. It offers some of the most beautiful vistas in southern Idaho. Occupancy: The following act is prohibited within the Minidoka Ranger District: Pursuant to 36 CFR 262.58 (a), camping in any area including a developed recreation site or an undeveloped/dispersed recreation site for more than 14 (fourteen) days in a 28 (twenty-eight) day period. A camper or a group of persons camping together must move off of National Forest lands within the Minidoka Ranger District for a minimum of 14 days after camping for 14 days. Campers who remain longer than 14 consecutive days and/or camp more than 14 days within a 28 day period may receive violation notices and fines under the authority described under Special Order Number: 0414-01-028. For more information contact the Minidoka Ranger District Office in Burley, ID—208-678-0430. No Horses are allowed in the campground. Limit 2 vehicles (autos) per site. Vehicles must be parked on gravel spurs provided. Do not park on the road; do not block traffic.

camps.name: Upper Penstemon Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Events Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Recreation Region: Minidoka Ranger District Upper Penstemon Campground Upper Penstemon Campground is located at the base of Magic Mountain Ski Area. This is a fee campground composed of 8 individual units and 1 group unit. Fee envelopes and a collection box are provided near the entrance and reservations are recommended. This area is accessible for a season that varies usually between June and September. Sites are handicapped accessible and campground amenities include a baseball diamond, horseshoe pits, and handicapped accessible toilets. The campground is well suited for motor homes, trailers, and tent camping. This area is popular in summer for trout fishing, hiking, and wildlife watching. There is a hiking trail at Elk Butte Spring that heads south to the Pike Mountain view point. Winter sports are popular from December to March and five cross-country ski trails that vary in length from 1.2 to 8.1 miles are located nearby. Three of these trails are groomed regularly. There are 55 miles of groomed snowmobile trails and another 350 miles of ungroomed marked routes. Magic Mountain Ski Resort boasts three lifts, accessing 14 runs. A large shelter and heated restrooms near the Diamondfield Jack parking area warms winter visitors. No water is available at this site.

camps.name: Warren Wagon Ranch
camps.description: Private, 4-stall barn located on the same fenced ranch property as our Warren Wagon Ranch Airbnb. It is available exclusively to registered Airbnb guests - we do not offer standalone boarding. Designed for traveling riders, this setup allows you to stay on-site with your horses in a clean, functional, and secure environment just minutes from downtown McCall. Barn Features: - Four fully enclosed 12' x 12' stalls - Rubber mats in each stall - Attached dry lot accessible from the barn - Insulated barn with electricity - Enclosed tack/feed room - Wash rack with hot and cold water - Maximum of 4 horses. Turnout Options - Guests may use: - Attached dry lot - 3-acre pasture - 0.5-acre pasture All turnout is use-at-your-own-risk. Primary fencing is post and rail. What to Bring: - Hay and feed (not provided) - Water buckets (general-use trough available) - Shavings (if desired) - Basic stall-cleaning tools. Guests are responsible for daily stall cleaning and manure disposal during their stay. Location notes: The property sits in open valley with mountain views, fenced perimeter, and ample trailer turnaround space, making it ideal for riders hauling in for trail riding, events, or extended McCall stays.

camps.name: White Sands Campground
camps.description: 2,100 foot elevation. 4 tent sites, 85 sites for tents or RVs, 2 group sites, and a playground on the Lochsa River. One campground loop is reserved for campers with horses and other stock. It has hitching rails, stock water, stock loading ramp and feeders. There is one trail outfitter at the campground. The campground is often visited by moose and other wildlife. The Lochsa River is popular in the spring for whitewater sports. There are a number of river accesses near the campground along US 12. Fishing for chinook salmon, steelhead, cutthroat and bull trout and mountain whitefish. Catch and release rules apply to some of these species; please check current regulations. Hiking or horseback riding on Boulder Creek Trail, Lochsa River Access Trail, Downriver Trail Scenic Overlook and Lochsa Park Trail. The Boulder Creek Trail leads to the Stanley Hot Springs, and most trails access the Bitterroot-Selway Wilderness.

camps.name: Whoop Um Up Campground (Equestrian)
camps.description: The Whoop-um-up Equestrian Campground is located 56 miles northeast of Boise, Idaho, along State Highway 21, under a scenic pine forested canopy. There are six campsites complete with feed boxes, hitching posts and water for stock. Wildlife and summer wildflowers are abundant. The historic town of Idaho City is just 11 miles south. The Crooked River runs near the site, offering rainbow trout fishing. Natural Features: State Highway 21, also known as the Ponderosa Pine Scenic Byway, snakes along Mores Creek to Mores Creek Summit, Gold Fork, and Banner Ridge with breathtaking views of the surrounding mountains and forest. The Crooked River runs near the campground offering an opportunity to catch a rainbow trout. Recreation: Numerous trail opportunities are in the area, offering hiking, biking and horseback riding. In the winter, the area becomes a playground for backcountry skiers and snowmobilers.

camps.name: Whoop Um Up Campground (Equestrian)
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Partially Closed Recreation Region: Idaho City Ranger District Whoop Um Up Campground (Equestrian) Current Conditions Campground accessible until closed by snow, but no water or toilet cleaning service provided. The Whoop-um-up Equestrian Campground is located 56 miles northeast of Boise, Idaho, along State Highway 21, under a scenic pine forested canopy. There are six campsites complete with feed boxes, picnic tables, a grill, fire ring, hitching posts, water for stock, and a vault restroom. Wildlife and summer wildflowers are abundant. The historic town of Idaho City is just 11 miles south. The Crooked River runs near the site, offering rainbow trout fishing. Numerous trail opportunities are in the area, offering hiking, biking and horseback riding. In the winter, the area becomes a playground for backcountry skiers and snowmobilers. The Upper Crooked River Trailhead includes visitor information. It serves Crooked River (#158) and Beaver Creek (#276) trails. Located not far from Edna Creek and Whoop Um Up Equestrian Campgrounds. For site specific questions, contact the Idaho City Ranger District.

camps.name: Whoop Um Up Trailhead
camps.description: The Whoop Um Up Trailhead includes a restroom and information kiosk. Fees are charged by the State in the winter, however the Forest Service operates it for free in summer. Located near Whoop Um Up Equestrian Campground and Edna Creek Campground.

camps.name: Wilderness Gateway Campground
camps.description: Wilderness Gateway Campground is one of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest’s premier campgrounds. Located at milepost 122.5 along the Northwest Passage Scenic Byway (US Highway 12), the campground offers 91 sites consisting of RV and tent camping, group camping, stock camping and facilities. The recreation area boasts its very own bird-watching trail, large trailhead parking for access into the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness, dump station, large picnic shelter and flush toilets, too.It also has picnic tables, fire rings, and toilets.. The Wilderness Gateway Campground has something for everyone: fishing, hiking, horseback riding, wildlife viewing, and don’t forget your camera! The scenery, wildlife and stunning Lochsa River are visions you won’t want to forget! The Campground will accomodate RV's up to 50-ft. length. Ut has some reservable sites. Loop A is a group site with 26 campsites and the whole loop must be reserved ahead of time. Loop B has 27 sites with 11 reservable sites. Loop C has 26 sites with 9 reservable sites. Loop D has 11 sites and 5 are reservable; this loop is reserved for stock camping only. The Dump Station is closed for the 2024 season Stock camping Loop D only. $14.00 per site with an 8 person site maximum. $2 per extra vehicle. Senior Passes are accepted.

camps.name: Willow Creek Transfer Camp
camps.description: Willow Creek Transfer Camp is composed of 3 large camping units. Campground amenities include picnic tables, fire rings, a restroom, corrals, mangers and barrier free stock loading ramps. The Willow Creek Trail No. 019 (single track trail) is located on the north end of the campground and is open to non-motorized travel as well as motorcycles. ATVs and UTVs are not allowed on the Willow Creek Trail.

camps.name: Willow Flat Campground
camps.description: T T T Alerts Current Conditions Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Epic Adventures Discover History Explore the Forest! Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Open Willow Flat Campground Willow Flat Campground is nestled along the banks of the Cub River, about seven miles southeast of Preston, Idaho. Tucked within the Caribou-Targhee National Forest in a scenic valley, this popular campground sits at an elevation of 6,300 feet, accessible via Cub River Road (Forest Road 406) off U.S. Highway 91. Natural Features: A mixed forest of pines, spruce, and hardwoods casts partial shade over the campground, while dense stands of willow line the Cub River’s banks, a favorite haunt of local moose. Deer and elk roam the surrounding hills, adding to the wild charm of this picturesque retreat framed by rugged mountains. Numerous trails begin within the campground, including a half-mile nature trail to Sam Parkinson Spring and the multi-use Cub River Trail, offering prime hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, and off-road vehicle adventures. The Cub River Trail connects to the renowned 55-mile Highline Trail, while the river itself provides excellent fishing for wild cutthroat and hatchery rainbow trout. Facilities: The campground offers six group sites accommodating 24 to 100 people and numerous single-family sites, each equipped with picnic tables and campfire rings. Vault toilets and drinking water are provided, and an amphitheater with bleacher seating and a cement platform sits at group site G03. Roads and parking spurs are gravel. Season: Late May-Early September After Season: Open, first-come/first-served; no fee, no toilets, no water. Willow Flat Campground

camps.name: Winding River Ranch, Silas Wilbur, 4043 US 95, PO 929
camps.description: Pasture boarding from 1+ acres to 60+ acres. Electric and Water hook ups for overnighters staying with their horses. Big Rig and Trailer parking available. Location notes: New Meadows, Idaho.

camps.name: Windy Saddle Horse Camp
camps.description: Located on Windy Saddle above the Hells Canyon Wilderness, the Windy Saddle Horse Camp is a small campground with 4 campsites. The campground has long camp spurs for trailers, an overflow parking area for stock trailers or day use, hitching rails and a loading ramp. Windy Saddle Trailhead General rules of use and restrictions apply for this developed recreation site. Wilderness Regulations apply within Hells Canyon Wildernes. • Motorized vehicles, bicycles, carts, hang glider and other mechanical equipment is prohibited in the Wilderness area. Overnight campsites fees are $10/night for single family unit (tent or trailer sites). Self-service pay station on site. Day Use Fees are $5/car/day parking/day use. Please use self-service pay station on site.

camps.name: Yellowjacket Lake Campground
camps.description: 8000-foot elevation. 7 campsites on Yellowjacket Lake, near the border of the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness. Sugarloaf Rock provides a fascinating and stunning backdrop for the lake. Trails from the campground go throughout the Yellowjacket Mountains and into the wilderness. Nearby trailside attractions are Hoodoo Meadows, McEleny Peak, and Yellowjacket Creek. Most area trails, except those in the wilderness, are open to multiple use. Fishing in the lake or in Yellowjacket Creek. Carry-down access for non-motorized boats to the lake. FR 113 is narrow with few turnouts. Not recommended for long RVs or cars with trailers. Travel is slow, passing can be difficult, and backing may be necessary. The nearby Yellowjacket Guard Station is accessed from FR 112 and is a reservable rental cabin. There is a corral for horses, a group fire ring, the Beagle Creek Trail, a woodstove for heat, and a gas cook stove. For more information or to reserve the Guard Station please visit Recreation.gov and search Yellowjacket Guard Station.

camps.name: Allen Quarter Horses, Kent & Dawn Allen
camps.description: We have a state of the art facility with 45 stalls. Big 12' x 12' stalls that are heated. Indoor arena available. RV hookups. Able to accommodate semi rigs. Some of the top trainers have stayed with us including Ted Turner, Jerry Wells, Tim McQuay, Dana Hokana, Clinton Anderson, Jim Searles, Gretchen Mathes and many more. Location notes: Just south of Effingham. 10 minutes off the interstate. Easy in and out.

camps.name: Altamont, Illinois, CAMPGROUND STABLES
camps.description: Just one-half mile off of Interstate 70, we offer a comfortable rest stop or an overnight stay for your horse(s). We also offer convenience! There's a turn-around drive, space for your trailer, plenty of room/pasture, wash bay, large clean stalls(16' x 16') with turnouts and a small picnic area for the family. $40 per horse per night. Restaurants, both fast food and sit down, as well as motels are close by. Location notes: Take the Altamont exit off of I-70(exit 82), go south 1/2 mile to Campground Road (watch for Town and Country Subdivision sign). Turn right on Campground Road. We're the second drive on the left.

camps.name: Annawan, Illinois, Klocken Fast Farm
camps.description: We are a small farm located just 3 miles off Interstate 80 in Annawan,Illinois. We have two barns totaling 8 stalls. The main building is a big Morton Building Barn with nice, clean, spacious stalls. We clean and sanitize the stalls after each guest stays. Use our water buckets or bring your own. We are ALL about the guest and VERY accommodating; whatever you need for you or your horse I promise we can make it happen! We have had many return guests for the simple fact that we are very accommodating. We also offer our round pen for overnight boarding which has become a favorite to allow your horse to stretch his legs and be outside for the night but still be in the safe enclosure of a nice, big 60 foot corral panel round pen. We have a water trough we put in there that's also cleaned and sanitized after every horse guest stays. Round pen overnight is $20 a horse and stall is $30 a horse. Even if you're using the stall you're welcome to turn your horse out in the round pen for as long as you please. There is a Best Western Hotel right in town so only 3 miles away; its a straight shot, no curvy long back roads. We also offer overnight hook up for $15 a night. We have a fire pit you're welcome to use and just enjoy yourself for the night; enjoy the stars and the quiet of the country! I always take pictures and update the owners on their horses if they choose to stay in the hotels:) Same day is normally always okay, and there is a $10 late fee arrival if after midnight. Hope to hear from you soon. Location notes: We are a small farm located about 3 miles off of Interstate 80 in Annawan, IL. No hassle to get here; easy on and off the interstate and the Best Western is right when you get off the Interstate.Please call or text with any questions.

Pasture also available. See AirBnb listing for photos, details and reviews. Coggins required. March to November only. Hay available. Location notes: Convenient to I-39.

camps.description: Private camp. Details may change; please confirm horse access, availability, amenities, fees, and rules before travel.

camps.name: Camp Cadiz Campground
camps.description: This campground is the site of an old Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) work camp. Somewhat off the beaten path Camp Cadiz is usually quiet and rarely do the campsites fill up; with the exception of turkey and deer hunting seasons. The campsites are level and each has a fire ring with grill and picnic table. Equestrian camping is allowed. Recreation Area brochure/map

camps.name: Cedar Creek Ranch
camps.description: Private camp. Details may change; please confirm horse access, availability, amenities, fees, and rules before travel.

camps.name: Cedar Lake Campground
camps.description: Our family campground offers the perfect getaway for nature-lovers and horse riders of all ages and levels. The 148 acre campground is bordered on two sides by the unparalleled beauty of the Shawnee National Forest, giving our campers direct access to unlimited hiking /riding trails and hunting opportunities. If that does not interest you, relax or fish by our twenty-five acre private lake or visit the scenic Southern Illinois Wine Trail. Come and experience a family camping trip like no other!

camps.description: Private camp. Details may change; please confirm horse access, availability, amenities, fees, and rules before travel.

camps.description: Private camp. Details may change; please confirm horse access, availability, amenities, fees, and rules before travel.

camps.name: Coyote Creek Stables, April Walk
camps.description: Coyote Creek offers overnight accommodations for horses & humans & pets. Only 10 minutes from Interstates 57 & 70 in Effingham & Neoga. Stay where the Budweiser Clydesdales and world famous barrel racer Fallon Taylor and Babyflo overnight. This is a perfect layover for trail riders also. Coyote Creek offers extra large 12' x 15' inside stalls, stalls with 25' runouts, 50' x 100' grassy paddocks and large pens with lean to shelters. Large indoor arena also available to stretch your horse's legs. Overnight room/apartment has a private entrance, 2 beds, bathroom, hot tub, patio and fire pit. 30 amp electric hookups for trailers and rvs. Semi and big trailer parking. Western store on site has 60+ saddles, tack and western apparel and gifts. Contact April 217-821-7783. Only 10 min from Interstates 57 & 70 in Effingham, IL and Neoga, IL. 10 minutes for restaurants. Location notes: 10 min. from Effingham, IL and Neoga, IL 20 min. from Mattoon, IL **From Effingham, IL I-57/70, take the Sigel exit #162, Turn North on Rt 45 through Sigel, At "Coyote Creek Tack" sign 2 miles north of Sigel, go west over railroad tracks. 1/2 mile, then right (north). First place on the right. **Neoga, IL I-57, take the Neoga exit #177, turn west (right), go through Neoga and five miles south of town. At "Coyote Creek Tack" sign, go right (west) over railroad tracks, 1/2 mile go right (north), first place on the right.

camps.description: Over 200 Campsites. Riding Right out of Camp. We Border the Shawnee on 3 Sides with direct forest trail access. 4 trailheads leaving camp. Huge, Marked, Mapped Trail System. Shawnee Forests only Wagon Trail. Trails End Grill Onsite. Open Weekends & Holidays March-Nov. (Free wi-fi) Outside Dining by the Fireplace, Beer,Cocktails&Wine available. Events Throughout the Year. Elec.& Water Hookups. RV Pads. Pull Through Sites. Large Primative Camping Area. Dumpstation. Heated & Air-conditioned Showerhouse. ATM on site. Propane Exchange. Ice. Pavillion. Playground. Cabins. Covered Stalls. Tie Line Poles.

camps.name: High Knob Ranch Equestrian Campground
camps.description: High Knob Ranch Campground is nestled inside the beautiful Shawnee National Forest, spread over 45 acres. Our 165 campsites consist of both permanent campsites and overnight campsites, which all include water and electricity. We are open year-round for your mule/horse riding pleasure!

camps.name: Horse Motel & Bunkhouse at Cement Hollow Equine Ctr
camps.location: 1974 Cement Hollow Road, East Carondelet , IL 62240
camps.description: Climate-controlled bunkhouse, loft above the bunkhouse, shower facilities. Indoor and outdoor riding arenas, paddocks, horse stalls, fans and a large parking lot for trailers. 2 camper hookups with 50, 30, and 20 amp service. Current health papers and proof of negative Coggins test are required. Arrivals by 8:00 p.m. please, unless previous arrangements have been made. 24 hour in advance reservations only. Call or text 314-312-9678 or e-mail patrgreg@gmail.com Click here to see our brochure with more details about our accomodations. Location notes: We are located in the rolling hills of southern Illinois and in close proximity to St. Louis, MO. Many of the St. Louis attractions, including the Arch and the highly acclaimed St. Louis Zoo, are located within 15 miles of the farm.

camps.name: Jim & Katie Troccoli
camps.description: Covered barn with three 12 x 12 stalls available, 50' round pen, hay available, limited trailer hook ups, plenty of room for big rigs. We have a three bedroom house on our ranch on Airbnb. We are the last horse ranch in Ottawa, Illinois. 7.92 acres with ranch house and barn are grandfathered into town. The barn price is not included in house rental. We live two blocks from the property. Location notes: Northern Illinois, easy access to Interstate 80.

camps.name: Little Lusk Trail Lodge Campground
camps.description: Little Lusk Campground & Lodge – Stonefort, Illinois Escape to the beauty of Southern Illinois at Little Lusk Campground & Lodge, a family-owned campground nestled in the heart of the Shawnee National Forest. Whether you’re looking for a peaceful weekend getaway, an outdoor adventure, or a place to make lifelong memories, Little Lusk has something for everyone. ✨ What You’ll Find: * Spacious campsites with primitive, electric, and full-hookup options * Beautiful stocked fishing ponds * Scenic horse trails with easy access to Shawnee National Forest * Horse stalls and an arena for equestrian guests * Clean bathhouse and modern amenities * A 6-bedroom, 8-bath lodge perfect for family reunions and group retreats * Event barn for weddings, reunions, and special events * Playground for the kids * Friendly, welcoming atmosphere where campers become family * Dog friendly 🌲 Adventure Awaits Located near Garden of the Gods, Bell Smith Springs, Jackson Falls, Pounds Hollow, and many of Southern Illinois’ most breathtaking hiking and outdoor destinations. 🎉 Fun All Season Long Enjoy family events throughout the camping season, including BBQ cook-offs, holiday celebrations, kids’ weekends, horse events, live music, campground games, and much more! At Little Lusk Campground & Lodge, you’re not just renting a campsite—you’re becoming part of a campground family. Come relax around the campfire, explore the trails, catch a fish, ride your horse, and make memories that will last a lifetime. Book your stay today! 📍 50 Barger Rd, Stonefort, IL 62987 📞 (270) 205-7138

camps.name: Maple Park, Illinois, C & M Clydesdales, LLC
camps.description: We are a small, family facility. We have 12' x 12' stalls, pasture with run-ins and paddocks. Prices and availability vary. There is a wash rack and outdoor arena available. Trailer parking is usually available. We don't have RV hookups but we do have water available. Location notes: We are three miles north of Elburn, Illinois, just off Highway 47. 12 miles north of I-88 on highway 47 or 16 miles south of I-90 on highway 47.

camps.name: Pine Tree Stables, Ron & Becky Althoff
camps.description: We offer overnight boarding for Equine travelers. We have large box stalls, 60' round pen, a 50' x 150' corral and a 100' x 150' corral. Camper electric hook-up and circle drive. All in a quiet setting. A large selection of motels and resturants are at exit 160. Location notes: At Effingham take exit 160 off of I-70/I-57. Go north on Route 32-33 for 2 miles. At the Dieterich Bank turn left onto Nazerene Road. Go 1 mile and turn left onto 1550th Ave. We are the first place on right. Althoff sign in yard.

camps.name: Pontoon Beach, Illinois, Gateway Stables
camps.description: St. Louis area's most convenient layover for you and your horse. Centrally located within minutes of all interstate highways and area attractions or hotels. Easy, no turn-around access for big rigs. Fuel and repair facilities nearby. Small family farm has big, clean stalls and/or safely fenced paddocks. Indoor/outdoor arenas. Stall bedding is included. We have plug-ins for RVS and trailers with living quarters. Top quality feed available for an extra charge. Lifelong horse people live on-site. Late arrivals or last minute arrangements are usually okay. Location notes: Within sight of St.Louis Arch, convenient to all interstate highways and hotels. South of 270, north of 55/70, west of 255. Five miles to Fairmount Park Racetrack (thoroughbreds).

camps.name: Rock N 4L Training Center, Rick Lacey
camps.location: 11255 North Sparrow Lane, Mt. Vernon , IL 62864
camps.description: We are a Quarter Horse and Thoroughbred training facility. We have 60+ 12' x 12' stalls or paddocks available 24/7. Cash only. Large turn around area and hook ups available. Check out our website for more pictures. Location notes: Interstates 64 and 57 combine in Mt.Vernon, IL. Get off of exit #95, go West about 1 Mile and turn Left (South) at the big green RP Lumber sign. Go appoximately 1 mile and the farm will be on the right hand side of the road.

camps.name: Rocky Road Arena, Rocky Wright
camps.description: We have 13 13' x 10 stalls' inside of a 80' x 140' indoor arena. $30 per horse per night. Stalls have lime and fresh shavings. Water faucets inside and hay available. Have buckets for feed and water or you may use your own. Round pen located just outside of arena. We have plenty of parking and room to turn around. Hookups for RV available. There is a motel in town and a few restaurants at which to eat. Coggins required. Location notes: About a mile off Interstate 24 Exit 14.

camps.name: Sommers Gate Farms, Lea Sommers
camps.description: Travelers seeking a place where they may stay on site with their horses will enjoy staying in their own rig at our campground or staying in our beautiful, new, huge, Grand Design Solitude 5th wheel camper with 5 slide outs. (The camper is unavailable from November 1st to April 1st but you are welcome to stay on site if you have a trailer with living quarters). The Grand Design comfortably sleeps up to 6 people and includes all the amenities of home: living room with 2 couches that fold out into double beds, 2 recliners, kitchen with dinette area, three-quarter bath, bedroom with king size bed, television, DVD player, towels and linens, dishes, coffee pot, microwave, toaster, stove, and residential refrigerator. We offer a 3-sided, 3-stall barn with 12' x 12' stalls that include mats and a paddock area. We also offer a new 4-stall horse barn with 12' x 12' stalls and mats. We can stable up to 7 horses. For travelers whose trailers have living quarters, campers, 5th wheels or motorhomes, our campsites are large and shady with 30 amp/ 50 amp hookups as well as access to water. We have a large parking lot that allows plenty of parking for trucks and trailers. We can accommodate big rigs. Pets are welcome. There is a port-a-potty on site. Our farm is about 12 miles north of Interstate 70; is very picturesque, peaceful and quiet. The nearest towns are Vandalia and Greenville. Both towns offer department stores, grocery stores, farm stores, hardware stores, banks, hospitals, and plenty of restaurants. For more information or to reserve a stay with us, call Lea Sommers at 618-593-0999 or email sommersgatefarms@gmail.com. The coffee is on us! Advance reservations are recommended. Location notes: GPS has a tendency to get people lost so the best advice is for you to call us for directions when you are getting close.

camps.name: TK Ranch Campground
camps.description: Campsite Descriptions All sites have 30A electric hookups, some with picnic table, and/or fire rings. Campsites have space available for 2-4 pens for your horses or mules.

camps.name: The Running Wilde Ranch
camps.description: 6-12' x 12' stalls with fans and 1-12' x 18' stall with fan. Large paddock or pasture w shelters available with pre-approval. Bedroom with private bathroom and entrance available with advance notice. Gated entrance - RV parking allowed right next horse barn with water hose hook up and 110 power outlet available- security cameras - reservation required. Hay available if needed. Health and Coggins required. Location notes: 15 miles from I-88. 20-25 miles from I-39, I-80, I-55. 60 miles west of Chicago.

camps.name: Triangle H Farm, Marcy Heepke
camps.description: At Triangle H Farm we have several 12' x 12' stalls with mats OR paddock turnout for the well-traveled equine. $20 per horse per night. Arrivals after 9 PM $10 late arrival fee. Custom care available to short or long-term boarders. Feed and hay available. Our facility includes outdoor arenas and round pen, indoor Cover-All fabric riding arena and hundreds of miles of trails. We offer English and western lessons for all ages and abilities. We will be hosting several horse shows each year as well as hunter paces, clinics, camps and an annual fall trail ride. We also have horses for sale/lease. Tack store open. Proud dealer of Timberline Saddles and Progressive Nutrition. We also sell Breyer Horses. See our web site for more information on the above topics as well as directions to our farm. Looking forward to meeting you! Location notes: Travel north on I-255 to Exit 6 which is the Woodriver/Edwardsville 143 Exit. Turn East (right) and go 1 mile to South Moreland Road. Turn North (left) on South Moreland and travel 1 mile. Our farm is on the left (West) side of the road. 1 hour southwest of Springfield, IL, 25 minutes northeast of St. Louis, MO.

camps.name: Victory Reigns Ranch Horse Hotel, and Bed and Breakfast
camps.description: Victory Reigns Ranch Horse Hotel and Bed and Breakfast boasts a beautiful ranch setting close to Deer Run Forest Preserve trails, Oak Ridge Forest Preserve trails and other equestrian trails. Come with or without your horse. We also have an RV hookup if needed along with spacious trailer and RV parking. 1 bedroom private apartment with full kitchen, bathroom, laundry in unit and living room. Satellite television and Wifi available. Stay for complimentary continental breakfast in the morning with your hosts. 7 acres of sprawling pasture and paddocks, dry lots, round pen, private turnout pasture, and 12' x 12' stalls with full mats and shavings fresh for your horse. Hay available for purchase for your stay. Dog friendly, but must be leashed on property and cleaned up after. Whether you are passing through for an equestrian event, looking for some R&R with your horse, or just looking to roast some marshmallows around the fire pit with good company, all are welcome at Victory Reigns Ranch. Location notes: Down the road from Baumann Park and right off of Hwy. I-90/39 and US 20. 10 miles from Boone county fairgrounds.

camps.name: Watson, Illinois, Freckled Pony Farm
camps.description: We are a friendly and welcoming facility that is dedicated to customizing accommodations suitable to your needs. 12' x 12' and 12' x 16' stalls with mats, as well as paddocks and pastures with run in sheds and automatic waterers await your stay. We have trailer hookup with both water and electric available and offer our very spacious camper if sleeping accommodations are needed. Amenities include a shoo fly system in the barn, an indoor and outdoor wash rack, indoor restroom complete with a shower, and a lounge where you can relax with a game, a good book, or some TV. Enjoy the beauty of the outdoors in our comfortable seating area featuring firepits and space for your kids and dogs to run and play. Guests are welcome to use our covered riding area as well as our outdoor arena when weather and ground conditions permit. Hungry? Add on a homemade meal for an additional cost or visit our little hometown restaurant or bar and grill. Hay is available for purchase for your stay / travel with prior notification. We take pride in ensuring a safe and comfortable environment for our guests and their equine. Please visit our website for additional information and prices. Location notes: 10 miles south of Effingham, IL, you will find a secure, 20 acres of completely fenced in beauty only 4 miles off Interstate 57 / 1.8 miles off Highway 37.
